_**The Bear**_ is an American [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") television series created by [Christopher Storer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Storer "Christopher Storer") for [FX on Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_on_Hulu "FX on Hulu"). [Jeremy Allen White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Allen_White "Jeremy Allen White") stars as [Carmy Berzatto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmy_Berzatto "Carmy Berzatto"), an award-winning chef who returns to his hometown of [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") to manage the chaotic kitchen at his recently deceased brother's [Italian beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_beef "Italian beef") sandwich shop. The regular cast includes [Ebon Moss-Bachrach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebon_Moss-Bachrach "Ebon Moss-Bachrach"), [Ayo Edebiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Edebiri "Ayo Edebiri"), [Lionel Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Boyce "Lionel Boyce"), [Liza Colón-Zayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liza_Col%C3%B3n-Zayas "Liza Colón-Zayas"), [Abby Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abby_Elliott "Abby Elliott"), [Matty Matheson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Matheson "Matty Matheson"), and [Edwin Lee Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Lee_Gibson "Edwin Lee Gibson").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-1)

The [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_1 "The Bear season 1") was released in its entirety on FX on Hulu on June 23, 2022. The [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_2 "The Bear season 2"), [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_3 "The Bear season 3") and [fourth seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_4 "The Bear season 4") were released in June 2023, June 2024, and June 2025, respectively. A standalone [special episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_(The_Bear_episode) "Gary (The Bear episode)") was released on May 5, 2026, starring Moss-Bachrach and [Jon Bernthal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Bernthal "Jon Bernthal"), and focused solely on their characters. The [fifth and final season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_5 "The Bear season 5") was released on June 25, 2026.

The series has received critical acclaim for its performances, writing, directing, visual style, soundtrack, and production values. Also, many real-life culinary professionals have praised the show for its sense of urgency and realistic depiction of the physical, emotional, and financial demands of restaurant life.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-4)_The Bear_ has received many accolades, including 22 [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") (including [Outstanding Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series")) and five [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") (including [Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Television_Series_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy")).

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

Talented [haute cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_cuisine "Haute cuisine") chef Carmy Berzatto inherits [his family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_on_The_Bear_(TV_series) "Family on The Bear (TV series)")'s Italian beef sandwich shop after his older brother [Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikey_Berzatto "Mikey Berzatto")'s suicide. He returns home to Chicago to run it, leaving behind his world of working in [Michelin-starred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin_Guide#Stars "Michelin Guide") restaurants. He is left to deal with his brother's unresolved debts, a rundown kitchen, and an unruly staff, while dealing with his own pain and family trauma.

## Cast and characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast and characters")]

Main article: [List of _The Bear_ characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Bear_characters "List of The Bear characters")

*   [Jeremy Allen White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Allen_White "Jeremy Allen White") as [Carmen "Carmy" Berzatto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmy_Berzatto "Carmy Berzatto"), also referred to as "Bear", an award-winning New York City [chef de cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef_de_cuisine "Chef de cuisine"), who returns to his hometown of Chicago to run his deceased brother Michael's failing [Italian beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_beef "Italian beef") restaurant, The Original Beef of Chicagoland (more commonly known as "The Beef"). Later, he converts The Beef to a [fine dining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_dining "Fine dining") restaurant called The Bear.
*   [Ebon Moss-Bachrach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebon_Moss-Bachrach "Ebon Moss-Bachrach") as [Richard "Richie" Jerimovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Jerimovich "Richie Jerimovich"), also referred to as "Cousin", Michael's best friend, the _[de facto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De\_facto "De facto")_ manager of the restaurant; later [maître d'hôtel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%C3%AEtre_d'h%C3%B4tel "Maître d'hôtel") of The Bear.
*   [Ayo Edebiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Edebiri "Ayo Edebiri") as [Sydney "Syd" Adamu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Adamu "Sydney Adamu"), a talented young chef who joins The Beef as its new [sous-chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sous-chef "Sous-chef") under Carmy.
*   [Lionel Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Boyce "Lionel Boyce") as [Marcus Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Brooks "Marcus Brooks"), The Beef's bread-baker-turned-pastry-chef, spurred on by Sydney's and Carmy's mentoring.
*   [Liza Colón-Zayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liza_Col%C3%B3n-Zayas "Liza Colón-Zayas") as [Tina Marrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Marrero "Tina Marrero"), an acerbic and stubborn line cook who eventually embraces the opportunity to train professionally.
*   [Abby Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abby_Elliott "Abby Elliott") as [Natalie "Sugar" Berzatto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalie_Berzatto "Natalie Berzatto"), Carmy's and Michael's sister, the reluctant co-owner and business manager of The Beef/The Bear.
*   [Matty Matheson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Matheson "Matty Matheson") as [Neil Fak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Bear_characters#Neil_Fak "List of The Bear characters") (seasons 2–5, recurring season 1), a quirky childhood friend of the Berzattos, and occasional handyman for the restaurant.

## Episodes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Episodes")]

The storyline of _The Bear_ is subdivided into parts marked by onscreen [title cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertitle "Intertitle"). The Part II title card appears in the first episode of season 2. The Part III title card appears in the first episode of season 3, which concludes with a "to be continued" card.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-6) Christopher Storer told reporters in 2023, "Season 2 is sort of where the show properly begins, once we've met everyone and seen their [backstory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstory "Backstory")."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-7) There is an [opening credits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_credits "Opening credits") sequence, each with a distinct [montage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montage_(filmmaking) "Montage (filmmaking)") and song selection, in episode 7 "Review," episode 14 "Fishes," episode 17 "Omelette," and episode 20 "Next." The [mean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean "Mean") running time is 35 minutes per episode.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-Lakkamraju-2026-8) The episode with the shortest runtime is "Review" (20 minutes).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-9) The longest episode is "Bears" (70 minutes).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S4Runtime-10)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Development")]

[FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") ordered a [pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot") for _The Bear_ in March 2021, to be written and directed by series creator [Christopher Storer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Storer "Christopher Storer").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-12) Storer had initially conceived _The Bear_ as a [feature film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_film "Feature film") before being convinced the story needed time to unreel.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) The pilot was filmed in July 2021.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-14) FX then ordered the series in October 2021 for a 2022 premiere.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-15) The sandwich shop interior is copied from the Chicago shop [Mr. Beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Beef "Mr. Beef") on Orleans Street, in [River North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_North "River North"). Storer was a frequent patron and is a friend of [Christopher Zucchero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Zucchero "Christopher Zucchero"), the shop's current owner who inherited it from his father.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-16)

In July 2022, the series was renewed for a 10-episode second season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-17) In November 2023, it was renewed for a third season.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-18) In March 2024, the series was renewed for a fourth season.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-19) Parts of the fourth season were filmed during filming for the third season, with production set to restart in 2025.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-21) In July 2025, it was renewed for a fifth and final season of eight episodes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S5Renewal-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)

### Writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Writing")]

The Bear of the title refers to an actual [bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear "Bear") that appears in a [dream sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_sequence "Dream sequence") in the [pilot episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot"), Carmy's nickname (derived from his surname), the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") and the [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs"), maybe the whole city [metonymically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonymic "Metonymic"), the name of the new restaurant, Carmy's girlfriend's nickname, the [collective noun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_noun "Collective noun") for the extended family, and/or maybe the bear is a metaphor for trauma.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-FOOTNOTENikolova202546-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESinger2026127-25) The situation is "family-owned restaurant," but, various sources argue, the show's themes are masculinity and father figures,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) team sports and collaboration,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-29) menswear and good taste,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-31) filmmaking and creativity,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-32) addiction and intergenerational transfer of maladaptive behaviors,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-34) the importance of a good wine list,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-35) the importance of strong institutions,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-36) the importance of regulatory easing for small business owners,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-38) gentrification and class warfare,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-41) Catholic mysticism,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-42) scars and ghosts and grief,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-43) women without men,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-44) mothers and women laboring,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-45) women in the workplace,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-47) dreams, and probably, possibly, maybe, love.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-48)

_Creative Screenwriting_ magazine wrote in 2025, "...the dialogue in _The Bear_ unfurls as poetry—a meditation, a stream of consciousness, a series of fragmented thoughts. It's messy, natural speech."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-49) The dialogue is rich with profanity—one reviewer described it as a "symphony of swearing."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-50)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Filming")]

The show films in Chicago, including on location in neighborhoods such as River North, [Ukrainian Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Village,_Chicago "Ukrainian Village, Chicago"), and [Wicker Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicker_Park,_Chicago "Wicker Park, Chicago"), and at real Chicago restaurants, including Mr. Beef, [Ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ever_(restaurant)#The_Bear "Ever (restaurant)"), and [Kasama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasama_(restaurant) "Kasama (restaurant)").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-51) Recurring visual and thematic motifs include time and trains.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-53) They typically shoot for "about 39 days" or an average of about four days per episode.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-54)

### Cinematography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Cinematography")]

The show's primary [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer") is [Andrew Wehde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wehde "Andrew Wehde").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-56) A-camera operator Gary Malouf and B-camera operator Chris Dame had both worked with Storer and Wehde on their previous projects.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-57) The show is shot with digital [Alexa Mini LF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexa_Mini_LF "Alexa Mini LF") cameras and [Panavision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panavision "Panavision") lenses.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-58) Two flashback episodes, "Fishes" and "Gary", were shot using film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-60) The show frequently uses handheld cameras.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-Panavision-S3-62)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Release")]

_The Bear_ premiered on [FX on Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_on_Hulu "FX on Hulu") in the United States on June 23, 2022,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-99) and became available internationally in the [Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_(Disney+) "Star (Disney+)") hub on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-100) The 10-episode second season was released on June 22, 2023.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premiere-101) Along with other [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") content, _The Bear_ became available to stream on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") in the U.S. via the Hulu hub on December 6, 2023.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-102) The third season was released on June 26, 2024.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S3Premiere-103) The fourth season was released on June 25, 2025.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-104) A surprise special flashback episode, "Gary", was released on May 5, 2026, on Hulu.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-105) The fifth season was released on June 25, 2026, on FX on Hulu, with a weekly broadcast on [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") beginning the same day,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S5FX-106) making it the first returning FX on Hulu series to receive a simultaneous broadcast on FX following a change in the latter's programming release strategy.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-107)

#### Season 1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Season 1")]

For the first season, Rotten Tomatoes reported an approval rating of 100% based on 82 critic reviews, with an average of rated review of 8.7/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "Like an expertly confected sandwich, _The Bear_ assembles a perfect melange of ingredients and stacks them for optimal satisfaction—and thankfully keeps the crust-iness for extra flavor."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS1-108) Metacritic gave it a weighted average score of 88 out of 100 based on 24 critic reviews.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS1-109)

The [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute") (AFI) named it [one of the ten best television programs of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute_Awards#2022 "American Film Institute Awards").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-AFI2022-129)_[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ named it number one of the best 100 TV shows of 2022 and described it as "the best workplace drama since _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-131)_The Bear_ appeared in the top 10 on numerous publications' "Best of 2022" lists, including first for _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_, _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_, _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_, and _[TVLine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVLine "TVLine")_, among others.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-132)

#### Season 2

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Season 2")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 99% of 112 critic reviews are positive, with an average of rated review of 9.3/10 for the second season. The site's critical consensus reads, "Instead of reinventing the menu, _The Bear_'s second season wisely opts to toss its lovable characters into another frying pan of adversity, lets 'em cook, and serves up yet another supremely satisfying dish."[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS2-110) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 92 out of 100 based on 43 critic reviews.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS2-111)

For the second year in a row, the AFI named _The Bear_ one of the ten best television programs of the year.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-133)_The Bear_ appeared on many publications' lists of the best TV shows of 2023, including _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_, and _People_, among others.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-134)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-135)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-136)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-137)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Season 3")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 89% of 103 critics gave the third season a positive review, with an average of rated review of 7.9/10. The website's critics consensus states, "Having set an exceedingly high standard of excellence for itself, _The Bear_ spends its third season simmering, stewing, and giving off an aroma that whets the appetite."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS3-112) The website also reported that the season was "as audacious as ever" and it "still seems to continue delivering compelling and often intense television with performances that are so dependably brilliant that they're not even mentioned in most of the reviews. Instead, at this point in a show's life, it's easier to find faults in its sameness or changes, or in its attempts to repeat or outdo itself."[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTES3-118) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 80 out of 100 based on 45 critic reviews.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS3-113)

#### Season 4

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Season 4")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 84% of 86 critics gave the fourth season a positive review, with an average of rated review of 7.3/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "After simmering for too long, _The Bear_'s fourth season finally turns the heat back up with a renewed sense of urgency, serving a rich meal despite tiresome wait times between courses."[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS4-114) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 72 out of 100 based on 40 critic reviews.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS4-115)

#### Season 5

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Season 5")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 97% of 77 critics gave the fifth season a positive review, with an average of rated reviews of 8.2/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "_The Bear_ closes out its final season with the character-driven finesse that it started with, ensuring its story and fans are served the finest of televisual meals without diminished returns."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS5-116) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 82 out of 100 based on 28 reviews.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS5-117)

_**The Bear**_ is an American [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") television series created by [Christopher Storer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Storer "Christopher Storer") for [FX on Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_on_Hulu "FX on Hulu"). [Jeremy Allen White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Allen_White "Jeremy Allen White") stars as [Carmy Berzatto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmy_Berzatto "Carmy Berzatto"), an award-winning chef who returns to his hometown of [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") to manage the chaotic kitchen at his recently deceased brother's [Italian beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_beef "Italian beef") sandwich shop. The regular cast includes [Ebon Moss-Bachrach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebon_Moss-Bachrach "Ebon Moss-Bachrach"), [Ayo Edebiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Edebiri "Ayo Edebiri"), [Lionel Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Boyce "Lionel Boyce"), [Liza Colón-Zayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liza_Col%C3%B3n-Zayas "Liza Colón-Zayas"), [Abby Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abby_Elliott "Abby Elliott"), [Matty Matheson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Matheson "Matty Matheson"), and [Edwin Lee Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Lee_Gibson "Edwin Lee Gibson").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-1)

The [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_1 "The Bear season 1") was released in its entirety on FX on Hulu on June 23, 2022. The [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_2 "The Bear season 2"), [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_3 "The Bear season 3") and [fourth seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_4 "The Bear season 4") were released in June 2023, June 2024, and June 2025, respectively. A standalone [special episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_(The_Bear_episode) "Gary (The Bear episode)") was released on May 5, 2026, starring Moss-Bachrach and [Jon Bernthal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Bernthal "Jon Bernthal"), and focused solely on their characters. The [fifth and final season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_season_5 "The Bear season 5") was released on June 25, 2026.

The series has received critical acclaim for its performances, writing, directing, visual style, soundtrack, and production values. Also, many real-life culinary professionals have praised the show for its sense of urgency and realistic depiction of the physical, emotional, and financial demands of restaurant life.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-4)_The Bear_ has received many accolades, including 22 [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") (including [Outstanding Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series")) and five [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") (including [Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Television_Series_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy")).

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

Talented [haute cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_cuisine "Haute cuisine") chef Carmy Berzatto inherits [his family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_on_The_Bear_(TV_series) "Family on The Bear (TV series)")'s Italian beef sandwich shop after his older brother [Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikey_Berzatto "Mikey Berzatto")'s suicide. He returns home to Chicago to run it, leaving behind his world of working in [Michelin-starred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin_Guide#Stars "Michelin Guide") restaurants. He is left to deal with his brother's unresolved debts, a rundown kitchen, and an unruly staff, while dealing with his own pain and family trauma.

## Cast and characters

Main article: [List of _The Bear_ characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Bear_characters "List of The Bear characters")

*   [Jeremy Allen White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Allen_White "Jeremy Allen White") as [Carmen "Carmy" Berzatto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmy_Berzatto "Carmy Berzatto"), also referred to as "Bear", an award-winning New York City [chef de cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef_de_cuisine "Chef de cuisine"), who returns to his hometown of Chicago to run his deceased brother Michael's failing [Italian beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_beef "Italian beef") restaurant, The Original Beef of Chicagoland (more commonly known as "The Beef"). Later, he converts The Beef to a [fine dining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_dining "Fine dining") restaurant called The Bear.
*   [Ebon Moss-Bachrach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebon_Moss-Bachrach "Ebon Moss-Bachrach") as [Richard "Richie" Jerimovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Jerimovich "Richie Jerimovich"), also referred to as "Cousin", Michael's best friend, the _[de facto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De\_facto "De facto")_ manager of the restaurant; later [maître d'hôtel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%C3%AEtre_d'h%C3%B4tel "Maître d'hôtel") of The Bear.
*   [Ayo Edebiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Edebiri "Ayo Edebiri") as [Sydney "Syd" Adamu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Adamu "Sydney Adamu"), a talented young chef who joins The Beef as its new [sous-chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sous-chef "Sous-chef") under Carmy.
*   [Lionel Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Boyce "Lionel Boyce") as [Marcus Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Brooks "Marcus Brooks"), The Beef's bread-baker-turned-pastry-chef, spurred on by Sydney's and Carmy's mentoring.
*   [Liza Colón-Zayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liza_Col%C3%B3n-Zayas "Liza Colón-Zayas") as [Tina Marrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Marrero "Tina Marrero"), an acerbic and stubborn line cook who eventually embraces the opportunity to train professionally.
*   [Abby Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abby_Elliott "Abby Elliott") as [Natalie "Sugar" Berzatto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalie_Berzatto "Natalie Berzatto"), Carmy's and Michael's sister, the reluctant co-owner and business manager of The Beef/The Bear.
*   [Matty Matheson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Matheson "Matty Matheson") as [Neil Fak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Bear_characters#Neil_Fak "List of The Bear characters") (seasons 2–5, recurring season 1), a quirky childhood friend of the Berzattos, and occasional handyman for the restaurant.
*   [Edwin Lee Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Lee_Gibson "Edwin Lee Gibson") as [Ebraheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebra "Ebra") (seasons 4–5, recurring seasons 1–3), a Somali veteran line cook at The Beef who is close with Tina.

## Episodes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Episodes")]

The storyline of _The Bear_ is subdivided into parts marked by onscreen [title cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertitle "Intertitle"). The Part II title card appears in the first episode of season 2. The Part III title card appears in the first episode of season 3, which concludes with a "to be continued" card.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-6) Christopher Storer told reporters in 2023, "Season 2 is sort of where the show properly begins, once we've met everyone and seen their [backstory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstory "Backstory")."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-7) There is an [opening credits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_credits "Opening credits") sequence, each with a distinct [montage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montage_(filmmaking) "Montage (filmmaking)") and song selection, in episode 7 "Review," episode 14 "Fishes," episode 17 "Omelette," and episode 20 "Next." The [mean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean "Mean") running time is 35 minutes per episode.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-Lakkamraju-2026-8) The episode with the shortest runtime is "Review" (20 minutes).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-9) The longest episode is "Bears" (70 minutes).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S4Runtime-10)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Development")]

[FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") ordered a [pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot") for _The Bear_ in March 2021, to be written and directed by series creator [Christopher Storer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Storer "Christopher Storer").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-12) Storer had initially conceived _The Bear_ as a [feature film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_film "Feature film") before being convinced the story needed time to unreel.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) The pilot was filmed in July 2021.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-14) FX then ordered the series in October 2021 for a 2022 premiere.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-15) The sandwich shop interior is copied from the Chicago shop [Mr. Beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Beef "Mr. Beef") on Orleans Street, in [River North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_North "River North"). Storer was a frequent patron and is a friend of [Christopher Zucchero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Zucchero "Christopher Zucchero"), the shop's current owner who inherited it from his father.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-16)

In July 2022, the series was renewed for a 10-episode second season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-17) In November 2023, it was renewed for a third season.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-18) In March 2024, the series was renewed for a fourth season.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-19) Parts of the fourth season were filmed during filming for the third season, with production set to restart in 2025.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-21) In July 2025, it was renewed for a fifth and final season of eight episodes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S5Renewal-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)

### Writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Writing")]

The Bear of the title refers to an actual [bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear "Bear") that appears in a [dream sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_sequence "Dream sequence") in the [pilot episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot"), Carmy's nickname (derived from his surname), the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") and the [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs"), maybe the whole city [metonymically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonymic "Metonymic"), the name of the new restaurant, Carmy's girlfriend's nickname, the [collective noun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_noun "Collective noun") for the extended family, and/or maybe the bear is a metaphor for trauma.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-FOOTNOTENikolova202546-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESinger2026127-25) The situation is "family-owned restaurant," but, various sources argue, the show's themes are masculinity and father figures,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) team sports and collaboration,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-29) menswear and good taste,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-31) filmmaking and creativity,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-32) addiction and intergenerational transfer of maladaptive behaviors,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-34) the importance of a good wine list,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-35) the importance of strong institutions,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-36) the importance of regulatory easing for small business owners,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-38) gentrification and class warfare,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-41) Catholic mysticism,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-42) scars and ghosts and grief,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-43) women without men,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-44) mothers and women laboring,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-45) women in the workplace,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-47) dreams, and probably, possibly, maybe, love.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-48)

_Creative Screenwriting_ magazine wrote in 2025, "...the dialogue in _The Bear_ unfurls as poetry—a meditation, a stream of consciousness, a series of fragmented thoughts. It's messy, natural speech."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-49) The dialogue is rich with profanity—one reviewer described it as a "symphony of swearing."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-50)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Filming")]

The show films in Chicago, including on location in neighborhoods such as River North, [Ukrainian Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Village,_Chicago "Ukrainian Village, Chicago"), and [Wicker Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicker_Park,_Chicago "Wicker Park, Chicago"), and at real Chicago restaurants, including Mr. Beef, [Ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ever_(restaurant)#The_Bear "Ever (restaurant)"), and [Kasama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasama_(restaurant) "Kasama (restaurant)").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-51) Recurring visual and thematic motifs include time and trains.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-53) They typically shoot for "about 39 days" or an average of about four days per episode.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-54)

### Cinematography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Cinematography")]

The show's primary [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer") is [Andrew Wehde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wehde "Andrew Wehde").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-56) A-camera operator Gary Malouf and B-camera operator Chris Dame had both worked with Storer and Wehde on their previous projects.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-57) The show is shot with digital [Alexa Mini LF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexa_Mini_LF "Alexa Mini LF") cameras and [Panavision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panavision "Panavision") lenses.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-58) Two flashback episodes, "Fishes" and "Gary", were shot using film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-60) The show frequently uses handheld cameras.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-Panavision-S3-62)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Release")]

_The Bear_ premiered on [FX on Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_on_Hulu "FX on Hulu") in the United States on June 23, 2022,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-99) and became available internationally in the [Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_(Disney+) "Star (Disney+)") hub on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-100) The 10-episode second season was released on June 22, 2023.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premiere-101) Along with other [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") content, _The Bear_ became available to stream on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") in the U.S. via the Hulu hub on December 6, 2023.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-102) The third season was released on June 26, 2024.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S3Premiere-103) The fourth season was released on June 25, 2025.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-104) A surprise special flashback episode, "Gary", was released on May 5, 2026, on Hulu.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-105) The fifth season was released on June 25, 2026, on FX on Hulu, with a weekly broadcast on [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") beginning the same day,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-S5FX-106) making it the first returning FX on Hulu series to receive a simultaneous broadcast on FX following a change in the latter's programming release strategy.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-107)

_The Bear_ has received critical acclaim.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-126) On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregation "Review aggregation") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the overall series holds a 93% rating, with an average of rated reviews of 8.3/10.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RT-127) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, the overall series has received a score of 83 out of 100.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MC-128)

#### Season 1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Season 1")]

For the first season, Rotten Tomatoes reported an approval rating of 100% based on 82 critic reviews, with an average of rated review of 8.7/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "Like an expertly confected sandwich, _The Bear_ assembles a perfect melange of ingredients and stacks them for optimal satisfaction—and thankfully keeps the crust-iness for extra flavor."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS1-108) Metacritic gave it a weighted average score of 88 out of 100 based on 24 critic reviews.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS1-109)

The [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute") (AFI) named it [one of the ten best television programs of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute_Awards#2022 "American Film Institute Awards").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-AFI2022-129)_[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ named it number one of the best 100 TV shows of 2022 and described it as "the best workplace drama since _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-131)_The Bear_ appeared in the top 10 on numerous publications' "Best of 2022" lists, including first for _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_, _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_, _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_, and _[TVLine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVLine "TVLine")_, among others.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-132)

#### Season 2

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Season 2")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 99% of 112 critic reviews are positive, with an average of rated review of 9.3/10 for the second season. The site's critical consensus reads, "Instead of reinventing the menu, _The Bear_'s second season wisely opts to toss its lovable characters into another frying pan of adversity, lets 'em cook, and serves up yet another supremely satisfying dish."[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS2-110) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 92 out of 100 based on 43 critic reviews.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS2-111)

For the second year in a row, the AFI named _The Bear_ one of the ten best television programs of the year.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-133)_The Bear_ appeared on many publications' lists of the best TV shows of 2023, including _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_, and _People_, among others.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-134)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-135)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-136)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-137)

#### Season 3

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Season 3")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 89% of 103 critics gave the third season a positive review, with an average of rated review of 7.9/10. The website's critics consensus states, "Having set an exceedingly high standard of excellence for itself, _The Bear_ spends its third season simmering, stewing, and giving off an aroma that whets the appetite."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS3-112) The website also reported that the season was "as audacious as ever" and it "still seems to continue delivering compelling and often intense television with performances that are so dependably brilliant that they're not even mentioned in most of the reviews. Instead, at this point in a show's life, it's easier to find faults in its sameness or changes, or in its attempts to repeat or outdo itself."[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTES3-118) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 80 out of 100 based on 45 critic reviews.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS3-113)

#### Season 4

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Season 4")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 84% of 86 critics gave the fourth season a positive review, with an average of rated review of 7.3/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "After simmering for too long, _The Bear_'s fourth season finally turns the heat back up with a renewed sense of urgency, serving a rich meal despite tiresome wait times between courses."[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS4-114) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 72 out of 100 based on 40 critic reviews.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS4-115)

#### Season 5

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Bear_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Season 5")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, 97% of 77 critics gave the fifth season a positive review, with an average of rated reviews of 8.2/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "_The Bear_ closes out its final season with the character-driven finesse that it started with, ensuring its story and fans are served the finest of televisual meals without diminished returns."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-RTS5-116) Metacritic assigned it a weighted average score of 82 out of 100 based on 28 reviews.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series)#cite_note-MCS5-117)

_**Blindspotting**_ is an American [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") television series and a [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)")[sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequel "Sequel") of the [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"). Set six months after the events of the film, the series follows Ashley, who is forced to move in with the mother of Miles, her boyfriend and father of her son, after he is suddenly incarcerated. The series co-stars [Jaylen Barron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Barron "Jaylen Barron"), Candace Nicholas-Lippman, Benjamin Earl Turner, and Atticus Woodward.

The series was created and executive produced by [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") and [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs"), writers, producers and lead stars of the original film, with Casal also acting as [showrunner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showrunner "Showrunner"). [Keith Calder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Calder "Keith Calder"), a producer on the original film, is also an executive producer, as well as actress [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones"). It premiered on June 13, 2021 on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-1) In October 2021, the series was renewed for a second season which premiered on April 14, 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3) In September 2023, the series was canceled after two seasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Six months after the events in the [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"), Miles, Ashley's partner of 12 years and father of their son, is suddenly incarcerated,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-5) and the situation leaves her to navigate a chaotic and humorous existential crisis when she and her son Sean are forced to move in with Miles' mother and half-sister.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-6)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Development")]

In September 2020, it was announced that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") had ordered a spin-off series of _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ by [Carlos López Estrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_L%C3%B3pez_Estrada "Carlos López Estrada"), with [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones") set to star and produce, with [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs") and [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") serving as executive producers and writers on the series.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-15) Production companies involved with the series were slated to consist of [Lionsgate Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Television "Lionsgate Television"), Snoot Entertainment, and Barnyard Projects.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-16) In December 2020, Benjamin Earl Turner, Atticus Woodward, Jaylen Barron, Candace Nicholas-Lippman and [Helen Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Hunt "Helen Hunt") joined the cast in starring roles, with Rafael Casal and [Justin Chu Cary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Chu_Cary "Justin Chu Cary") set to appear in recurring capacity.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") for the series began in December 2020.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-19) Production for the first season took place in March 2021 in [West Oakland, Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Oakland,_Oakland,_California "West Oakland, Oakland, California").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)

Diggs does not reprise his film role as Collin in the first season beyond a voice cameo in the finale, despite co-creating the show. Casal hoped to include Collin during the planning stages, but Diggs wished for the season to focus on Ashley. He ultimately came to regret not making an appearance. Diggs and Casal both expressed interest in bringing back Collin for a potential second season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-21)

On October 14, 2021, Starz renewed the series for a second season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2) On April 14, 2022, [LeVar Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeVar_Burton "LeVar Burton"), Katlynn Simone Smith, Tamera Tomakili, and [Tim Chantarangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Chantarangsu "Tim Chantarangsu") were cast in recurring roles, while [E-40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-40 "E-40"), [P-Lo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_HBK_Gang "The HBK Gang") and [Too $hort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too_$hort "Too $hort") were set to guest star for the second season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Recurandguest-7) Production for the series' sophomore season wrapped on April 28, 2022.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-22)

It was announced on January 11, 2023 that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") would premiere a number of episodes of their sophomore season at the 2023 [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") Festival held in Austin, Texas in March under the TV Spotlight category.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)

On September 25, 2023, Starz canceled the series after two seasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Music")]

Show creators Rafael Casal and Daveed Diggs recruited fellow schoolmate [Ambrose Akinmusire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambrose_Akinmusire "Ambrose Akinmusire") and _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ film composer [Michael Yezerski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Yezerski "Michael Yezerski") to compose the score for the series. Akinmusire and Yezerski have created score to accompany spoken word, verse, dance, and various other types of scenes demonstrated throughout the series. In a _Variety_ article, Akinmusire and Yezerski describe the experience as "a very rare opportunity for the score to just become the driving language of a piece of dramatic television content."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-24)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Release")]

The series had its world premiere at the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") on June 11, 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Tribeca-9)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-25) It premiered on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") on June 13, 2021.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-26) The second season premiered on April 14, 2023.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the first season holds an approval rating of 100% based on 25 critic reviews, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "The rare adaptation that exceeds its source material, _Blindspotting_ deftly takes on complicated social constructs with comedic flair, crafting a show that's as funny as it is poignant while giving its incredible ensemble—led by the captivating Jasmine Cephas Jones—plenty of room to shine."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a weighted average score of 76 out of 100, based on 15 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)

The second season has a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 5 critic reviews, with an average rating of 8.7/10.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-29)

_**Blindspotting**_ is an American [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") television series and a [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)")[sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequel "Sequel") of the [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"). Set six months after the events of the film, the series follows Ashley, who is forced to move in with the mother of Miles, her boyfriend and father of her son, after he is suddenly incarcerated. The series co-stars [Jaylen Barron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Barron "Jaylen Barron"), Candace Nicholas-Lippman, Benjamin Earl Turner, and Atticus Woodward.

The series was created and executive produced by [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") and [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs"), writers, producers and lead stars of the original film, with Casal also acting as [showrunner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showrunner "Showrunner"). [Keith Calder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Calder "Keith Calder"), a producer on the original film, is also an executive producer, as well as actress [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones"). It premiered on June 13, 2021 on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-1) In October 2021, the series was renewed for a second season which premiered on April 14, 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3) In September 2023, the series was canceled after two seasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Six months after the events in the [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"), Miles, Ashley's partner of 12 years and father of their son, is suddenly incarcerated,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-5) and the situation leaves her to navigate a chaotic and humorous existential crisis when she and her son Sean are forced to move in with Miles' mother and half-sister.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-6)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Development")]

In September 2020, it was announced that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") had ordered a spin-off series of _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ by [Carlos López Estrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_L%C3%B3pez_Estrada "Carlos López Estrada"), with [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones") set to star and produce, with [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs") and [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") serving as executive producers and writers on the series.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-15) Production companies involved with the series were slated to consist of [Lionsgate Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Television "Lionsgate Television"), Snoot Entertainment, and Barnyard Projects.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-16) In December 2020, Benjamin Earl Turner, Atticus Woodward, Jaylen Barron, Candace Nicholas-Lippman and [Helen Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Hunt "Helen Hunt") joined the cast in starring roles, with Rafael Casal and [Justin Chu Cary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Chu_Cary "Justin Chu Cary") set to appear in recurring capacity.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") for the series began in December 2020.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-19) Production for the first season took place in March 2021 in [West Oakland, Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Oakland,_Oakland,_California "West Oakland, Oakland, California").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)

Diggs does not reprise his film role as Collin in the first season beyond a voice cameo in the finale, despite co-creating the show. Casal hoped to include Collin during the planning stages, but Diggs wished for the season to focus on Ashley. He ultimately came to regret not making an appearance. Diggs and Casal both expressed interest in bringing back Collin for a potential second season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-21)

On October 14, 2021, Starz renewed the series for a second season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2) On April 14, 2022, [LeVar Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeVar_Burton "LeVar Burton"), Katlynn Simone Smith, Tamera Tomakili, and [Tim Chantarangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Chantarangsu "Tim Chantarangsu") were cast in recurring roles, while [E-40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-40 "E-40"), [P-Lo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_HBK_Gang "The HBK Gang") and [Too $hort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too_$hort "Too $hort") were set to guest star for the second season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Recurandguest-7) Production for the series' sophomore season wrapped on April 28, 2022.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-22)

It was announced on January 11, 2023 that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") would premiere a number of episodes of their sophomore season at the 2023 [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") Festival held in Austin, Texas in March under the TV Spotlight category.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)

On September 25, 2023, Starz canceled the series after two seasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Music")]

Show creators Rafael Casal and Daveed Diggs recruited fellow schoolmate [Ambrose Akinmusire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambrose_Akinmusire "Ambrose Akinmusire") and _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ film composer [Michael Yezerski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Yezerski "Michael Yezerski") to compose the score for the series. Akinmusire and Yezerski have created score to accompany spoken word, verse, dance, and various other types of scenes demonstrated throughout the series. In a _Variety_ article, Akinmusire and Yezerski describe the experience as "a very rare opportunity for the score to just become the driving language of a piece of dramatic television content."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-24)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Release")]

The series had its world premiere at the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") on June 11, 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Tribeca-9)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-25) It premiered on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") on June 13, 2021.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-26) The second season premiered on April 14, 2023.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the first season holds an approval rating of 100% based on 25 critic reviews, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "The rare adaptation that exceeds its source material, _Blindspotting_ deftly takes on complicated social constructs with comedic flair, crafting a show that's as funny as it is poignant while giving its incredible ensemble—led by the captivating Jasmine Cephas Jones—plenty of room to shine."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a weighted average score of 76 out of 100, based on 15 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)

The second season has a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 5 critic reviews, with an average rating of 8.7/10.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-29)

_**Kevin Can F**k Himself**_[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-1) is an American [dark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_comedy "Dark comedy")[comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama") television series created by Valerie Armstrong, who also serves as an executive producer. The title is a parody of the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom _[Kevin Can Wait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin\_Can\_Wait "Kevin Can Wait")_.

The first two episodes were made available on [AMC+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC+ "AMC+") on June 13, 2021, and the series premiered on [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") on June 20, 2021.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-Futon-2) In August 2021, the series was renewed for a second season. In November 2021, AMC confirmed the series would end after two seasons. The second and final season premiered on August 22, 2022, on AMC and AMC+.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-Screenrant-3)

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

Set in [Worcester, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_Massachusetts "Worcester, Massachusetts"), the show explores the life of Allison McRoberts, a woman struggling to redefine her life amid an unhappy marriage to her husband, Kevin, an egocentric man-child whose cruel and manipulative treatment of her is [domestic abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_abuse "Domestic abuse"). The show presents contrasting perspectives of her experience—a typical [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") wife when Allison is with her husband, shown with a [multiple-camera setup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple-camera_setup "Multiple-camera setup") and [canned laughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laugh_track "Laugh track"), and as a woman navigating a difficult personal path, filmed in the [single-camera setup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-camera_setup "Single-camera setup") more common to television dramas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4)

### Main

*   [Annie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Murphy "Annie Murphy") as Allison Devine McRoberts, a housewife seeking to take the lead in her own life after a decade of trying to be a perfect wife.
*   [Mary Hollis Inboden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Hollis_Inboden "Mary Hollis Inboden") as Patricia Deirdre "Patty" O'Connor, the McRoberts' neighbor who owns a hair salon. *   [Eric Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Petersen "Eric Petersen") as Kevin McRoberts, an insensitive and unambitious man-child who is Allison's husband—modeled on the loutish husbands in [sitcoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") such as _[The King of Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_King\_of\_Queens "The King of Queens")_, _[The Honeymooners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Honeymooners "The Honeymooners")_, and, most pointedly, _[Kevin Can Wait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin\_Can\_Wait "Kevin Can Wait")_, the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom starring [Kevin James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James "Kevin James").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-5) He is completely oblivious to Allison's life and activities when she is away from him.
*   Alex Bonifer as Neil O'Connor, Kevin's friend and Patty's brother. During Season 1, he is mostly a side character in the "sitcom" segments as the naive, devoted best friend sidekick character. He is more involved in the reality segments during Season 2, becoming incredibly unstable and eventually disillusioned with Kevin's behavior.
*   [Brian Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Howe_(actor) "Brian Howe (actor)") as Peter "Pete" McRoberts, Kevin's father. He predominantly makes caustic comments on the goings-on in the "sitcom" portions of the show and often gets involved in his son's activities.
*   [Raymond Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lee_(actor) "Raymond Lee (actor)") as Samuel "Sam" Park, Allison's old friend from high school who now owns a diner and is married. He and Allison still have feelings for each other.
*   Candice Coke as Detective Tammy Ridgeway (main season 2; recurring season 1), a detective investigating illegal oxycodone distribution; she enters into a relationship with Patty in season 1.
