Later at a bar, Neil retorts that he is sick of Kevin's mistreatment and tells him to leave, breaking off their friendship. Patty kicks Neil out of the house. Neil confesses his love to Diane; she rebuffs him, stating it is not her job to make him a better person, but she encourages him to get his life together for his own sake. Allison returns to Worcester and warns Molly about Kevin's behavior. Later, when Kevin tells a disconcerted Molly to move in with him, she abruptly leaves. Allison returns home and tells Kevin that she wants a divorce. Kevin is initially confused, then reacts violently, threatening to ruin her life. After Allison leaves, Kevin drinks heavily and begins to burn Allison's belongings; he calls Pete, Neil, and Molly, leaving them increasingly vicious and hateful verbally abusive voicemails after not one of them takes his calls. After Kevin passes out in a drunken stupor, the fire spreads and engulfs the house, which is witnessed by the whole neighborhood, including Patty and Neil. With Kevin dead, Patty sits on the steps of the now burned-down house and is joined by Allison; they tearfully embrace, and Allison reveals that she wants to stay in Worcester. They both pledge to "die alone together" as they watch the sunrise, ready for a new future without Kevin. **Guest star**: [Erinn Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erinn_Hayes "Erinn Hayes") |

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Development")]

In November 2018, it was announced [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") had opened a writers' room on the series as part of its scripts-to-series development model, with Valerie Armstrong serving as creator and executive producer, with [Rashida Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashida_Jones "Rashida Jones") and [Will McCormack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_McCormack "Will McCormack") serving as executive producers under their Le Train Train banner.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-21) In October 2019, AMC ordered the series.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-22)

The show's title is an allusion to _[Kevin Can Wait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin\_Can\_Wait "Kevin Can Wait")_, a 2016 [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom starring [Kevin James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James "Kevin James"), which was heavily criticized for the manner in which the lead character's wife (played by [Erinn Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erinn_Hayes "Erinn Hayes")) was written out of the show in the second season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4) Although _Kevin Can F**k Himself_ is not meant as a direct parody of _Kevin Can Wait_, that incident served as a jumping-off point for the creative team of _Kevin Can F**k Himself_ to make a show exploring the implications of gender roles in American family sitcoms.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4) On August 27, 2021, AMC renewed the series for a second season.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-S2Renewal-23) On November 30, 2021, AMC confirmed the series would conclude after two seasons.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-24)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Casting")]

In February 2020, [Annie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Murphy "Annie Murphy") joined the series' cast in the leading role.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-25) In March 2020, [Eric Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Petersen "Eric Petersen"), [Mary Hollis Inboden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Hollis_Inboden "Mary Hollis Inboden") and Alex Bonifer joined the cast in starring roles.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-26) In May 2020, [Raymond Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lee_(actor) "Raymond Lee (actor)") and [Brian Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Howe_(actor) "Brian Howe (actor)") also joined the cast in starring roles.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-27) In January 2021, Meghan Leathers and Candice Coke joined the cast in recurring roles.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-28)

In May 2022, Erinn Hayes from _Kevin Can Wait_ was cast in a guest role.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-29)

### Shooting Locations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Shooting Locations")]

The McRoberts house exteriors were shot on Nason Street in [Brockton, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brockton,_Massachusetts "Brockton, Massachusetts"). Other shooting locations around Massachusetts include Worcester, [Hingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hingham,_Massachusetts "Hingham, Massachusetts"), [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Massachusetts "Milton, Massachusetts"), [Randolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph,_Massachusetts "Randolph, Massachusetts"), [Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton,_Massachusetts "Canton, Massachusetts"), Common Market Restaurants in [Quincy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy,_Massachusetts "Quincy, Massachusetts"), and in Brockton the Campello Station of the [United States Postal Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Postal_Service "United States Postal Service") and the First Evangelical Lutheran Church.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-30)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

The first season of _Kevin Can F**k Himself_ holds an 82% approval rating on [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 60 reviews with an average rating of 6.80/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_Kevin Can F**k Himself_'s ambitious blend of genres don't always gel, but searing social commentary and a stellar performance from Annie Murphy make for an engaging watch."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-31) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the first season holds a rating of 65 out of 100, based on 25 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-32)

On Rotten Tomatoes, the second season holds an approval rating of 100% with an average rating of 7.7/10 based on 7 reviews.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-33)

### Accolades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Accolades")]

The first season episode "Live Free or Die" won the [American Cinema Editors Award for Best Edited Multi-Camera Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Cinema_Editors_Award_for_Best_Edited_Multi-Camera_Comedy_Series "American Cinema Editors Award for Best Edited Multi-Camera Comedy Series"), with "Fixed" and "The Grand Victorian" also nominated.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-AmericanCinemaEditors2022-34) The series was recognized with [The ReFrame Stamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp "The ReFrame Stamp") for hiring people of underrepresented gender identities, and of color.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-ReFrame-35) In [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/38th_Artios_Awards "38th Artios Awards"), the series was nominated by the [Casting Society of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casting_Society_of_America "Casting Society of America") for the Outstanding Achievement in Casting - Television Pilot and First Season - Drama Artios award.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-36)

_**Kevin Can F**k Himself**_[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-1) is an American [dark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_comedy "Dark comedy")[comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama") television series created by Valerie Armstrong, who also serves as an executive producer. The title is a parody of the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom _[Kevin Can Wait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin\_Can\_Wait "Kevin Can Wait")_.

The first two episodes were made available on [AMC+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC+ "AMC+") on June 13, 2021, and the series premiered on [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") on June 20, 2021.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-Futon-2) In August 2021, the series was renewed for a second season. In November 2021, AMC confirmed the series would end after two seasons. The second and final season premiered on August 22, 2022, on AMC and AMC+.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-Screenrant-3)

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

Set in [Worcester, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_Massachusetts "Worcester, Massachusetts"), the show explores the life of Allison McRoberts, a woman struggling to redefine her life amid an unhappy marriage to her husband, Kevin, an egocentric man-child whose cruel and manipulative treatment of her is [domestic abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_abuse "Domestic abuse"). The show presents contrasting perspectives of her experience—a typical [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") wife when Allison is with her husband, shown with a [multiple-camera setup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple-camera_setup "Multiple-camera setup") and [canned laughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laugh_track "Laugh track"), and as a woman navigating a difficult personal path, filmed in the [single-camera setup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-camera_setup "Single-camera setup") more common to television dramas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4)

### Main

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Main")]

*   [Annie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Murphy "Annie Murphy") as Allison Devine McRoberts, a housewife seeking to take the lead in her own life after a decade of trying to be a perfect wife.
*   [Mary Hollis Inboden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Hollis_Inboden "Mary Hollis Inboden") as Patricia Deirdre "Patty" O'Connor, the McRoberts' neighbor who owns a hair salon. In the sitcom sections she acts as the tomboyish, tough, "honorary guy" member of Kevin's friends whom they often forget is a girl.
*   [Eric Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Petersen "Eric Petersen") as Kevin McRoberts, an insensitive and unambitious man-child who is Allison's husband—modeled on the loutish husbands in [sitcoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") such as _[The King of Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_King\_of\_Queens "The King of Queens")_, _[The Honeymooners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Honeymooners "The Honeymooners")_, and, most pointedly, _[Kevin Can Wait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin\_Can\_Wait "Kevin Can Wait")_, the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom starring [Kevin James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James "Kevin James").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-5) He is completely oblivious to Allison's life and activities when she is away from him.
*   Alex Bonifer as Neil O'Connor, Kevin's friend and Patty's brother. During Season 1, he is mostly a side character in the "sitcom" segments as the naive, devoted best friend sidekick character. He is more involved in the reality segments during Season 2, becoming incredibly unstable and eventually disillusioned with Kevin's behavior.
*   [Brian Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Howe_(actor) "Brian Howe (actor)") as Peter "Pete" McRoberts, Kevin's father. He predominantly makes caustic comments on the goings-on in the "sitcom" portions of the show and often gets involved in his son's activities.
*   [Raymond Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lee_(actor) "Raymond Lee (actor)") as Samuel "Sam" Park, Allison's old friend from high school who now owns a diner and is married. He and Allison still have feelings for each other.
*   Candice Coke as Detective Tammy Ridgeway (main season 2; recurring season 1), a detective investigating illegal oxycodone distribution; she enters into a relationship with Patty in season 1.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Development")]

In November 2018, it was announced [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") had opened a writers' room on the series as part of its scripts-to-series development model, with Valerie Armstrong serving as creator and executive producer, with [Rashida Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashida_Jones "Rashida Jones") and [Will McCormack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_McCormack "Will McCormack") serving as executive producers under their Le Train Train banner.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-21) In October 2019, AMC ordered the series.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-22)

The show's title is an allusion to _[Kevin Can Wait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin\_Can\_Wait "Kevin Can Wait")_, a 2016 [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom starring [Kevin James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James "Kevin James"), which was heavily criticized for the manner in which the lead character's wife (played by [Erinn Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erinn_Hayes "Erinn Hayes")) was written out of the show in the second season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4) Although _Kevin Can F**k Himself_ is not meant as a direct parody of _Kevin Can Wait_, that incident served as a jumping-off point for the creative team of _Kevin Can F**k Himself_ to make a show exploring the implications of gender roles in American family sitcoms.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-chaney-4) On August 27, 2021, AMC renewed the series for a second season.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-S2Renewal-23) On November 30, 2021, AMC confirmed the series would conclude after two seasons.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-24)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Casting")]

In February 2020, [Annie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Murphy "Annie Murphy") joined the series' cast in the leading role.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-25) In March 2020, [Eric Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Petersen "Eric Petersen"), [Mary Hollis Inboden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Hollis_Inboden "Mary Hollis Inboden") and Alex Bonifer joined the cast in starring roles.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-26) In May 2020, [Raymond Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lee_(actor) "Raymond Lee (actor)") and [Brian Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Howe_(actor) "Brian Howe (actor)") also joined the cast in starring roles.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-27) In January 2021, Meghan Leathers and Candice Coke joined the cast in recurring roles.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-28)

In May 2022, Erinn Hayes from _Kevin Can Wait_ was cast in a guest role.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-29)

### Shooting Locations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Shooting Locations")]

The McRoberts house exteriors were shot on Nason Street in [Brockton, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brockton,_Massachusetts "Brockton, Massachusetts"). Other shooting locations around Massachusetts include Worcester, [Hingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hingham,_Massachusetts "Hingham, Massachusetts"), [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Massachusetts "Milton, Massachusetts"), [Randolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph,_Massachusetts "Randolph, Massachusetts"), [Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton,_Massachusetts "Canton, Massachusetts"), Common Market Restaurants in [Quincy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy,_Massachusetts "Quincy, Massachusetts"), and in Brockton the Campello Station of the [United States Postal Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Postal_Service "United States Postal Service") and the First Evangelical Lutheran Church.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-30)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

The first season of _Kevin Can F**k Himself_ holds an 82% approval rating on [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 60 reviews with an average rating of 6.80/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_Kevin Can F**k Himself_'s ambitious blend of genres don't always gel, but searing social commentary and a stellar performance from Annie Murphy make for an engaging watch."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-31) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the first season holds a rating of 65 out of 100, based on 25 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-32)

On Rotten Tomatoes, the second season holds an approval rating of 100% with an average rating of 7.7/10 based on 7 reviews.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-33)

### Accolades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Accolades")]

The first season episode "Live Free or Die" won the [American Cinema Editors Award for Best Edited Multi-Camera Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Cinema_Editors_Award_for_Best_Edited_Multi-Camera_Comedy_Series "American Cinema Editors Award for Best Edited Multi-Camera Comedy Series"), with "Fixed" and "The Grand Victorian" also nominated.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-AmericanCinemaEditors2022-34) The series was recognized with [The ReFrame Stamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp "The ReFrame Stamp") for hiring people of underrepresented gender identities, and of color.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-ReFrame-35) In [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/38th_Artios_Awards "38th Artios Awards"), the series was nominated by the [Casting Society of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casting_Society_of_America "Casting Society of America") for the Outstanding Achievement in Casting - Television Pilot and First Season - Drama Artios award.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Can_F**k_Himself#cite_note-36)

_**A Good Girl's Guide to Murder**_ is a British [mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_fiction "Mystery fiction")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)") television series based on [the 2019 novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder") by [Holly Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Jackson "Holly Jackson"), adapted by Poppy Cogan, directed by [Dolly Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Wells "Dolly Wells"), and developed by Moonage Pictures and the German public broadcaster [ZDFneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDFneo "ZDFneo") for [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three"). The series, consisting of six episodes, covers events from the first book, and premiered on 1 July 2024 on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") in the United Kingdom, followed by its terrestrial premiere on BBC Three on 10 July. It was released internationally on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on 1 August 2024.

The second series was released on 27 May 2026. A third and final series is set to premiere in 2027.

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

Teenage sleuth Pippa "Pip" Fitz-Amobi ([Emma Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Myers "Emma Myers")) is not satisfied with the police's handling of cases in her small English town, Little Kilton, and investigates, while producing her [EPQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Project_Qualification "Extended Project Qualification") and podcast on it.

The first season revolves around the killing of Andie Bell, a student at Pippa "Pip" Fitz- Amobi's school. She was assumed to have been murdered by her boyfriend, Sal Singh, who seemingly committed suicide shortly after. Pip investigates further to clear Sal's name and gets closer to his brother, Ravi ([Zain Iqbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zain_Iqbal "Zain Iqbal")), whose family was ostracized after Sal was accused of killing Andie.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-2)

The second season revolves around the disappearance of Pip's best friend Connor's brother, Jamie. Connor pleads with Pip to help in the search for Jamie, who was last seen at a memorial for Sal and Andie, a few days before he is to appear as a witness in court. Pip investigates and helps spread awareness about Jamie's disappearance through episodes of her podcast.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-3)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Production")]

In September 2022, the project was announced as a [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three") television adaptation of the [Holly Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Jackson "Holly Jackson") novel _[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Good\_Girl's\_Guide\_to\_Murder "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder")_, produced by Moonage Pictures.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-5)[Dolly Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Wells "Dolly Wells") is a director on the project from a script by Poppy Cogan, alongside Zia Ahmed, Ajoke Ibironke, and Ruby Thomas. It is produced by Florence Walker, and executive producers include Matthew Read, Matthew Bouch and Frith Tiplady for Moonage Pictures, and Lucy Richer and Danielle Scott-Haughton for the BBC, along with Wells, Holly Jackson, and Cogan.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-6)

Despite the executive producer Frith Tiplady stressing that the first series has a real end,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-8) it was renewed for a second series on 20 November 2024, which adapts the second book, _Good Girl, Bad Blood_. Jackson and Cogan returned to write the screenplay while Myers and Iqbal reprised their respective roles.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-9) In June 2026, a third and final series was confirmed to have already been filmed, which will adapt the third book, _As Good As Dead_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-FinalSeries-10)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Casting")]

In June 2023, production started with [Emma Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Myers "Emma Myers") and [Zain Iqbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zain_Iqbal "Zain Iqbal") cast into the lead roles of Pip and Ravi.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-12)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Filming")]

Filming took place around [Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol "Bristol") and [Somerset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerset "Somerset"). Locations include the [Redcliffe Caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redcliffe_Caves "Redcliffe Caves"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) the [Avon Valley Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avon_Valley_Railway "Avon Valley Railway") car park,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-14)[Redland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redland,_Bristol "Redland, Bristol"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-redlandandwestbury-15)[Redmaids' High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redmaids'_High_School "Redmaids' High School"), [Westbury-on-Trym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westbury-on-Trym "Westbury-on-Trym"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-redlandandwestbury-15) and [Axbridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axbridge "Axbridge").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-filmloc-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-redlandandwestbury-15) Filming for the second series took place in the final week of April 2025 in Axbridge, Somerset.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-18)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Release")]

_A Good Girl's Guide to Murder_ premiered on 1 July 2024 on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") in the United Kingdom[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-filmloc-17)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-tellymix-19) and in Ireland,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)[Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_(streaming_service) "Stan (streaming service)") in Australia,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-21) and [ThreeNow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ThreeNow "ThreeNow") in New Zealand.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-22) A terrestrial broadcast on [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three") began on 10 July 2024,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-tellymix-19) with two episodes being broadcast per week.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-23) The series was released in Germany on 30 August 2024 on the [ZDFmediathek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDF "ZDF") service, while [ZDFneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDFneo "ZDFneo") broadcast two episodes per week beginning from 8 September 2024.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-24) The series was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on 1 August 2024.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-netflixreleasedate-25)

The second series was released on BBC iPlayer and ZDFmediathek on 27 May 2026. The third and final series is set to be released in 2027.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-FinalSeries-10)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reception")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 83% of 41 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.4/10.The website's consensus reads: "A frothy series that carries off the classic murder mystery with a light touch, _A Good Girl's Guide to Murder'_ s checks all the boxes for a sweetly satisfying binge."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-26)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned a score of 69 out of 100, based on 20 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-27)

For the second series, 92% of 13 critics' reviews on Rotten Tomatoes are positive, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's consensus reads: "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder returns for a darker, more narratively rich season two, weaving a new web of intrigue that Emma Myers embraces with aplomb."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)

_**A Good Girl's Guide to Murder**_ is a British [mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_fiction "Mystery fiction")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)") television series based on [the 2019 novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder") by [Holly Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Jackson "Holly Jackson"), adapted by Poppy Cogan, directed by [Dolly Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Wells "Dolly Wells"), and developed by Moonage Pictures and the German public broadcaster [ZDFneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDFneo "ZDFneo") for [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three"). The series, consisting of six episodes, covers events from the first book, and premiered on 1 July 2024 on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") in the United Kingdom, followed by its terrestrial premiere on BBC Three on 10 July. It was released internationally on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on 1 August 2024.

The second series was released on 27 May 2026. A third and final series is set to premiere in 2027.

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

Teenage sleuth Pippa "Pip" Fitz-Amobi ([Emma Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Myers "Emma Myers")) is not satisfied with the police's handling of cases in her small English town, Little Kilton, and investigates, while producing her [EPQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Project_Qualification "Extended Project Qualification") and podcast on it.

The first season revolves around the killing of Andie Bell, a student at Pippa "Pip" Fitz- Amobi's school. She was assumed to have been murdered by her boyfriend, Sal Singh, who seemingly committed suicide shortly after. Pip investigates further to clear Sal's name and gets closer to his brother, Ravi ([Zain Iqbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zain_Iqbal "Zain Iqbal")), whose family was ostracized after Sal was accused of killing Andie.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-2)

The second season revolves around the disappearance of Pip's best friend Connor's brother, Jamie. Connor pleads with Pip to help in the search for Jamie, who was last seen at a memorial for Sal and Andie, a few days before he is to appear as a witness in court. Pip investigates and helps spread awareness about Jamie's disappearance through episodes of her podcast.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-3)

Before he could be charged Sal allegedly confessed to killing Andie and then took his own life. However, Pip believes that Sal was innocent and is determined to find out the truth. After initially being rebuffed by Sal's brother Ravi, she begins her investigation by interviewing Sal's friend Naomi Ward, the older sister of Pip's best friend Cara, whose father Elliot is an English teacher at their school. Naomi reveals that Sal had an alibi for the night of Andie's disappearance, though doesn't elaborate after their conversation is interrupted. Following an interview with Sal's friend Max Hastings, who claims Naomi is lying to protect Sal, she approaches Ravi again. ## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Production")]

In September 2022, the project was announced as a [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three") television adaptation of the [Holly Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Jackson "Holly Jackson") novel _[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Good\_Girl's\_Guide\_to\_Murder "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder")_, produced by Moonage Pictures.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-5)[Dolly Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Wells "Dolly Wells") is a director on the project from a script by Poppy Cogan, alongside Zia Ahmed, Ajoke Ibironke, and Ruby Thomas. It is produced by Florence Walker, and executive producers include Matthew Read, Matthew Bouch and Frith Tiplady for Moonage Pictures, and Lucy Richer and Danielle Scott-Haughton for the BBC, along with Wells, Holly Jackson, and Cogan.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-6)

Despite the executive producer Frith Tiplady stressing that the first series has a real end,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-8) it was renewed for a second series on 20 November 2024, which adapts the second book, _Good Girl, Bad Blood_. Jackson and Cogan returned to write the screenplay while Myers and Iqbal reprised their respective roles.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-9) In June 2026, a third and final series was confirmed to have already been filmed, which will adapt the third book, _As Good As Dead_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-FinalSeries-10)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Casting")]

In June 2023, production started with [Emma Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Myers "Emma Myers") and [Zain Iqbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zain_Iqbal "Zain Iqbal") cast into the lead roles of Pip and Ravi.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-12)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Filming")]

Filming took place around [Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol "Bristol") and [Somerset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerset "Somerset"). Locations include the [Redcliffe Caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redcliffe_Caves "Redcliffe Caves"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) the [Avon Valley Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avon_Valley_Railway "Avon Valley Railway") car park,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-14)[Redland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redland,_Bristol "Redland, Bristol"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-redlandandwestbury-15)[Redmaids' High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redmaids'_High_School "Redmaids' High School"), [Westbury-on-Trym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westbury-on-Trym "Westbury-on-Trym"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-redlandandwestbury-15) and [Axbridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axbridge "Axbridge").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-filmloc-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-redlandandwestbury-15) Filming for the second series took place in the final week of April 2025 in Axbridge, Somerset.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-18)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Release")]

_A Good Girl's Guide to Murder_ premiered on 1 July 2024 on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") in the United Kingdom[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-filmloc-17)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-tellymix-19) and in Ireland,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)[Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_(streaming_service) "Stan (streaming service)") in Australia,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-21) and [ThreeNow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ThreeNow "ThreeNow") in New Zealand.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-22) A terrestrial broadcast on [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three") began on 10 July 2024,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-tellymix-19) with two episodes being broadcast per week.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-23) The series was released in Germany on 30 August 2024 on the [ZDFmediathek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDF "ZDF") service, while [ZDFneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDFneo "ZDFneo") broadcast two episodes per week beginning from 8 September 2024.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-24) The series was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on 1 August 2024.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-netflixreleasedate-25)

The second series was released on BBC iPlayer and ZDFmediathek on 27 May 2026. The third and final series is set to be released in 2027.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-FinalSeries-10)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Good_Girl%27s_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reception")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 83% of 41 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.4/10.The website's consensus reads: "A frothy series that carries off the classic murder mystery with a light touch, _A Good Girl's Guide to Murder'_ s checks all the boxes for a sweetly satisfying binge."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-26)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned a score of 69 out of 100, based on 20 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-27)

For the second series, 92% of 13 critics' reviews on Rotten Tomatoes are positive, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's consensus reads: "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder returns for a darker, more narratively rich season two, weaving a new web of intrigue that Emma Myers embraces with aplomb."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Girl's_Guide_to_Murder_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)

**David A. Carter** (born March 4, 1957) is an American [author](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Author "Author") and [illustrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illustrator "Illustrator"). He is best known for his [pop-up books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop-up_book "Pop-up book") for both children and adults. His _Bugs_ series has sold over 6 million copies.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_A._Carter&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

During the late 1970s, Carter worked as a [graphic designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphic_designer "Graphic designer") and advertising illustrator. Until 1987 he worked as an artist, a paper engineer and a book designer for a publishing house. After this he moved into his current career as an author, illustrator, and paper engineer, primarily of children's books. His first book was _How Many Bugs in a Box?_. Carter often works with his wife, Noelle Carter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-2) Carter has created more than 90 books, including a guide on how to make pop-ups titled, _The Elements of Pop Up_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-3) He designed a [hardback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcover "Hardcover") book of graffiti design for the British band [Coldplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coldplay "Coldplay")'s 2011 album [Mylo Xyloto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mylo_Xyloto "Mylo Xyloto").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-4)

Carter and paper engineer James Diaz were awarded the 2023 Meggendorfer Prize for Best Paper Engineering at the 15th annual [Movable Book Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movable_Book_Society "Movable Book Society") Conference in Cleveland, Ohio.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-5)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_A._Carter&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Carter was born on 4 March 1957, at the L.D.S. Hospital in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-6) He attended [Utah State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_State_University "Utah State University"). His hobbies include gardening, tennis, skiing and travelling.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He lives with his wife, Noelle L. Carter in [Auburn, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn,_California "Auburn, California"). They have two daughters, Molly and Emma.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-8)

**David A. Carter** (born March 4, 1957) is an American [author](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Author "Author") and [illustrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illustrator "Illustrator"). He is best known for his [pop-up books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop-up_book "Pop-up book") for both children and adults. His _Bugs_ series has sold over 6 million copies.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_A._Carter&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

During the late 1970s, Carter worked as a [graphic designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphic_designer "Graphic designer") and advertising illustrator. Until 1987 he worked as an artist, a paper engineer and a book designer for a publishing house. After this he moved into his current career as an author, illustrator, and paper engineer, primarily of children's books. His first book was _How Many Bugs in a Box?_. Carter often works with his wife, Noelle Carter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-2) Carter has created more than 90 books, including a guide on how to make pop-ups titled, _The Elements of Pop Up_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-3) He designed a [hardback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcover "Hardcover") book of graffiti design for the British band [Coldplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coldplay "Coldplay")'s 2011 album [Mylo Xyloto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mylo_Xyloto "Mylo Xyloto").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-4)

Carter and paper engineer James Diaz were awarded the 2023 Meggendorfer Prize for Best Paper Engineering at the 15th annual [Movable Book Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movable_Book_Society "Movable Book Society") Conference in Cleveland, Ohio.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-5)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_A._Carter&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Carter was born on 4 March 1957, at the L.D.S. Hospital in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-6) He attended [Utah State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_State_University "Utah State University"). His hobbies include gardening, tennis, skiing and travelling.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He lives with his wife, Noelle L. Carter in [Auburn, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn,_California "Auburn, California"). They have two daughters, Molly and Emma.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Carter#cite_note-8)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American film and television director (born 1973)

**Seith Mann** (born 1973)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) is an American film and television director. He directed the short film _Five Deep Breaths_ (2003) and has gone on to direct episodes of _[The Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wire\_(TV\_series) "The Wire (TV series)")_, _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ and _[Fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe\_(TV\_series) "Fringe (TV series)")_.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Mann was inspired to become a director when he saw the [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee") film _[Do the Right Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_the\_Right\_Thing "Do the Right Thing")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise2-2) Mann graduated from [Morehouse College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morehouse_College "Morehouse College") and later earned an MFA in film at the [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts") at [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)

### Five Deep Breaths

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Five Deep Breaths")]

Mann's thesis at New York University was the short film _Five Deep Breaths_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) It was awarded the Spike Lee fellowship while in development in 2002.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Florida_Film_Festival-4) The film is set at an all-black college. After a physical assault upon a young woman by her boyfriend, another man, Mark, and his friends are moved to take revenge.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Vulture_Picture_Palace-5) Mann has commented that he likes morally ambiguous situations.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) The short starred [Jamie Hector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Hector "Jamie Hector"), [Anslem Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anslem_Richardson "Anslem Richardson"), Marcuis Harris, Harvey Gardner Moore, Curtiss Cook, and Ka'ramuu Kush. The score was composed by jazz musician [Jason Moran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Moran_(musician) "Jason Moran (musician)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)

The film premiered at the 2003 [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) It won first place in the Charles and Lucille King Family Foundation Award (for Best Short Film[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)), and The Carl Lerner Award for Film with Social Significance at the 2003 New York University First Run Festival. It was selected to screen at the 2003 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") and one of four American shorts to screen at the Cinefondation Competition at the 2003 [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) It won a Gold Plaque for Narrative Short Film at the 2003 [Chicago International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_International_Film_Festival "Chicago International Film Festival").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-39th_Chicago_International_Film_Festival_Winners-6) It also won the Best Narrative Short Film award at the 2003 Los Angeles IFP/West Film Festival.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Movie_City_News-7)

Film maker magazine named Mann one of their 25 new faces of independent film in 2003.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) They praised his direction of _Five Short Breaths_ as "skillful".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) The IFP gave Mann the Gordon Parks Awards for Emerging African-American Filmmakers following the film's release.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-IFP_Press_Release-8)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Television")]

Television Producer [Robert F. Colesberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Colesberry "Robert F. Colesberry") saw _Five Deep Breaths_ and introduced the other producers of HBO drama _[The Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wire "The Wire")_ to it.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) The producers approached Mann and asked him to shadow their directors during production of the third season in 2004.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) Show runner [David Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Simon_(writer) "David Simon (writer)") recalls that Colesberry wanted Mann to direct a third season episode but Colesberry's untimely death left the other producers reeling and they felt unable to risk a directorial debut in their first season without him.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9) Simon recalls Mann shadowing director [Ernest R. Dickerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_R._Dickerson "Ernest R. Dickerson") and showing a "careful interest in the process."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9)

In 2006, Mann joined the directing crew of _The Wire'_ s fourth season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-The_Wire_season_4_crew-10) Simon felt obligated to give Mann a chance after his dedication to shadowing Dickerson.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9) Mann made his television directing debut with the third episode of the season, "[Home Rooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Rooms_(The_Wire_episode) "Home Rooms (The Wire episode)")".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-E40-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-EG40-12) Simon was pleased with the episode and described it as "beautifully covered."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9)

Mann also was an ABC DGA Fellow class of 2005, a fellowship aimed at encouraging "diversity of race, gender and spirit in the filmmaking community."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-The_Futon_Critic-13) In 2007 Mann was nominated for an NAACP Image Award in the category Outstanding Directing in a Dramatic Series for his work on episode "Home Rooms".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter_Image_2007-14) Mann has commented that he was "excited" to receive the nomination and grateful to the NAACP for their work.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)

After _The Wire_, Mann worked on _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ directing two episodes in 2006, "The Name of the Game" and "Don't Stand So Close to Me". In 2007, Mann was nominated for a [DGA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DGA_Award "DGA Award") in the category Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Comedy Series for his work on "The Name of the Game".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Variety_DGA-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Variety_2007_DGA-16) Mann has also directed episodes of _[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_(American\_TV\_series) "Heroes (American TV series)")_, _[Cold Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Case "Cold Case")_, _[Lincoln Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln\_Heights\_(TV\_series) "Lincoln Heights (TV series)")_, _[Jericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jericho\_(2006\_TV\_series) "Jericho (2006 TV series)")_, _[Entourage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entourage\_(U.S.\_TV\_series) "Entourage (U.S. TV series)")_, _[Friday Night Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday\_Night\_Lights\_(TV\_series) "Friday Night Lights (TV series)")_, _[Men in Trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men\_in\_Trees "Men in Trees")_, _[Shark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark\_(U.S.\_TV\_series) "Shark (U.S. TV series)")_, _[Fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe\_(TV\_series) "Fringe (TV series)"), [Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting\_(TV\_series) "Blindspotting (TV series)"),_ and _[The Walking Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Walking\_Dead\_(TV\_series) "The Walking Dead (TV series)")_.

### Future projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Future projects")]

Mann is working on a feature film script entitled _Come Sunday_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) The script won two development awards (the Emerging Narrative Screenwriting Award and the Gordon Parks Award for Screenwriting) from the IFP in 2004.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-IndieWIRE-17) In 2010, Mann was announced as director of _Miss: Better Living Through Crime_ with [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee") producing.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-18) In 2016, Mann was writing the _Black_ movie.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-19)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American film and television director (born 1973)

**Seith Mann** (born 1973)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) is an American film and television director. He directed the short film _Five Deep Breaths_ (2003) and has gone on to direct episodes of _[The Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wire\_(TV\_series) "The Wire (TV series)")_, _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ and _[Fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe\_(TV\_series) "Fringe (TV series)")_.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Mann was inspired to become a director when he saw the [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee") film _[Do the Right Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_the\_Right\_Thing "Do the Right Thing")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise2-2) Mann graduated from [Morehouse College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morehouse_College "Morehouse College") and later earned an MFA in film at the [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts") at [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)

### Five Deep Breaths

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Five Deep Breaths")]

Mann's thesis at New York University was the short film _Five Deep Breaths_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) It was awarded the Spike Lee fellowship while in development in 2002.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Florida_Film_Festival-4) The film is set at an all-black college. After a physical assault upon a young woman by her boyfriend, another man, Mark, and his friends are moved to take revenge.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Vulture_Picture_Palace-5) Mann has commented that he likes morally ambiguous situations.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) The short starred [Jamie Hector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Hector "Jamie Hector"), [Anslem Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anslem_Richardson "Anslem Richardson"), Marcuis Harris, Harvey Gardner Moore, Curtiss Cook, and Ka'ramuu Kush. The score was composed by jazz musician [Jason Moran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Moran_(musician) "Jason Moran (musician)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)

The film premiered at the 2003 [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) It won first place in the Charles and Lucille King Family Foundation Award (for Best Short Film[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3)), and The Carl Lerner Award for Film with Social Significance at the 2003 New York University First Run Festival. It was selected to screen at the 2003 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") and one of four American shorts to screen at the Cinefondation Competition at the 2003 [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) It won a Gold Plaque for Narrative Short Film at the 2003 [Chicago International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_International_Film_Festival "Chicago International Film Festival").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-39th_Chicago_International_Film_Festival_Winners-6) It also won the Best Narrative Short Film award at the 2003 Los Angeles IFP/West Film Festival.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Movie_City_News-7)

Film maker magazine named Mann one of their 25 new faces of independent film in 2003.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) They praised his direction of _Five Short Breaths_ as "skillful".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Film_Maker-3) The IFP gave Mann the Gordon Parks Awards for Emerging African-American Filmmakers following the film's release.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-IFP_Press_Release-8)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Television")]

Television Producer [Robert F. Colesberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Colesberry "Robert F. Colesberry") saw _Five Deep Breaths_ and introduced the other producers of HBO drama _[The Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wire "The Wire")_ to it.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) The producers approached Mann and asked him to shadow their directors during production of the third season in 2004.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) Show runner [David Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Simon_(writer) "David Simon (writer)") recalls that Colesberry wanted Mann to direct a third season episode but Colesberry's untimely death left the other producers reeling and they felt unable to risk a directorial debut in their first season without him.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9) Simon recalls Mann shadowing director [Ernest R. Dickerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_R._Dickerson "Ernest R. Dickerson") and showing a "careful interest in the process."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9)

In 2006, Mann joined the directing crew of _The Wire'_ s fourth season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-The_Wire_season_4_crew-10) Simon felt obligated to give Mann a chance after his dedication to shadowing Dickerson.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9) Mann made his television directing debut with the third episode of the season, "[Home Rooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Rooms_(The_Wire_episode) "Home Rooms (The Wire episode)")".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-E40-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-EG40-12) Simon was pleased with the episode and described it as "beautifully covered."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Jim_King_David_Simon_interview_3-9)

Mann also was an ABC DGA Fellow class of 2005, a fellowship aimed at encouraging "diversity of race, gender and spirit in the filmmaking community."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-The_Futon_Critic-13) In 2007 Mann was nominated for an NAACP Image Award in the category Outstanding Directing in a Dramatic Series for his work on episode "Home Rooms".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter_Image_2007-14) Mann has commented that he was "excited" to receive the nomination and grateful to the NAACP for their work.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)

After _The Wire_, Mann worked on _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ directing two episodes in 2006, "The Name of the Game" and "Don't Stand So Close to Me". In 2007, Mann was nominated for a [DGA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DGA_Award "DGA Award") in the category Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Comedy Series for his work on "The Name of the Game".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Variety_DGA-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Variety_2007_DGA-16) Mann has also directed episodes of _[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_(American\_TV\_series) "Heroes (American TV series)")_, _[Cold Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Case "Cold Case")_, _[Lincoln Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln\_Heights\_(TV\_series) "Lincoln Heights (TV series)")_, _[Jericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jericho\_(2006\_TV\_series) "Jericho (2006 TV series)")_, _[Entourage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entourage\_(U.S.\_TV\_series) "Entourage (U.S. TV series)")_, _[Friday Night Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday\_Night\_Lights\_(TV\_series) "Friday Night Lights (TV series)")_, _[Men in Trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men\_in\_Trees "Men in Trees")_, _[Shark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark\_(U.S.\_TV\_series) "Shark (U.S. TV series)")_, _[Fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe\_(TV\_series) "Fringe (TV series)"), [Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting\_(TV\_series) "Blindspotting (TV series)"),_ and _[The Walking Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Walking\_Dead\_(TV\_series) "The Walking Dead (TV series)")_.

### Future projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seith_Mann&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Future projects")]

Mann is working on a feature film script entitled _Come Sunday_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-Black_Enterprise-1) The script won two development awards (the Emerging Narrative Screenwriting Award and the Gordon Parks Award for Screenwriting) from the IFP in 2004.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-IndieWIRE-17) In 2010, Mann was announced as director of _Miss: Better Living Through Crime_ with [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee") producing.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-18) In 2016, Mann was writing the _Black_ movie.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seith_Mann#cite_note-19)

_**The Shards**_ is an American [teen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-2) television series for [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") and [FX on Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_on_Hulu "FX on Hulu"). It premiered on August 5, 2026. The series was created by [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(producer) "Ryan Murphy (producer)") and [Bret Easton Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bret_Easton_Ellis "Bret Easton Ellis"), based on Ellis's [semi-autobiographical novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards "The Shards").

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

The series is set in Los Angeles in 1981. The story follows a 17-year-old version of [Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bret_Easton_Ellis "Bret Easton Ellis") during his final year at the elite [Buckley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckley_School_(California) "Buckley School (California)") prep school. Upending the character's world is the arrival of a mysterious new student, Robert Mallory, whose unsettling presence coincides with the activities of a serial killer known as The Trawler.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Release-3)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Development")]

In April 2023, it was reported that Ellis would write the series based on his novel for [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO"), with Ellis executive producing alongside Nick Hall and Brian Young.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-12) In a June 2023 interview with the Spanish publication _El Independiente_, Ellis had confirmed that [Luca Guadagnino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luca_Guadagnino "Luca Guadagnino") was set to direct the series with Ellis himself saying that he may direct some episodes as well.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) In January 2025, Ellis revealed that the adaptation, which [Kristoffer Borgli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristoffer_Borgli "Kristoffer Borgli") had signed on to direct, was no longer being developed at HBO, following creative differences. In February 2025, [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(producer) "Ryan Murphy (producer)") was revealed to be in closing talks to revive the project at a different network.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-14)

In May 2025, it was announced that [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") was in early development on the series and it would be directed by [Max Winkler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Winkler_(director) "Max Winkler (director)"). It is produced by [20th Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Television "20th Television") in association with Ryan Murphy Television. Murphy, Ellis and Winkler executive produce alongside Nick Hall, Kathleen McCaffrey, [Michael Uppendahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Uppendahl "Michael Uppendahl"), Brian Young, [Alexis Martin Woodall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Martin_Woodall "Alexis Martin Woodall"), [Nina Jacobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Jacobson "Nina Jacobson"), [Brad Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Simpson_(producer) "Brad Simpson (producer)"), [Braxton Pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braxton_Pope "Braxton Pope"), and Tanase Popa.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Release-3)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Gerber-15) In July 2025, the series was officially greenlit.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Series_Order-16) Murphy has talked about a plan for the show to run for at least 3 seasons.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-17)

Prior to the series order, [Jacob Elordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Elordi "Jacob Elordi") was reported to be in talks for a role in the adaption in September 2023. ## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Release")]

In March 2026, [Brad Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Simpson_(producer) "Brad Simpson (producer)") revealed in an interview that _The Shards_ had been aiming for a summer airdate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) In June 2026, it was announced that the series would premiere on August 5, 2026.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Release-3)[FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") and [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") released the first two episodes of the series on August 5, with the remaining episodes released weekly on Wednesdays through the season finale on September 9.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-28) Internationally, _The Shards_ was made available for streaming on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-29)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On the review aggregator website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 56% of 57 critics' reviews are positive, with an average of rated reviews of 6.3/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "The combination of [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(producer) "Ryan Murphy (producer)") and [Bret Easton Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bret_Easton_Ellis "Bret Easton Ellis") should elicit magnanimously pulpy TV, but instead _The Shards_ relegates itself to obtuse style with mildly entertaining substance."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-RT-30)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 55 out of 100, based on 24 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-31)

### Ratings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Ratings")]

On streaming, _The Shards_ ranked No. 2 on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu")'s "Top 15 Today" list—a daily updated list of the platform's most-watched titles—on August 6, the day after its premiere. The series remained on Hulu's "Top 15 Today" list from August 6 through September 18, 2026.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-38) Streaming analytics firm FlixPatrol, which monitors daily updated VOD charts and streaming ratings across the globe, reported that _The Shards_ ranked No. 1 as the most-streamed series worldwide on Disney+ on August 15, 2026. On the same day, the series was notably the most-streamed series on Disney+ in countries including Albania, Australia, Belgium, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, and New Zealand.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-39)

_**The Shards**_ is an American [teen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-2) television series for [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") and [FX on Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_on_Hulu "FX on Hulu"). It premiered on August 5, 2026. The series was created by [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(producer) "Ryan Murphy (producer)") and [Bret Easton Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bret_Easton_Ellis "Bret Easton Ellis"), based on Ellis's [semi-autobiographical novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards "The Shards").

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

The series is set in Los Angeles in 1981. The story follows a 17-year-old version of [Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bret_Easton_Ellis "Bret Easton Ellis") during his final year at the elite [Buckley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckley_School_(California) "Buckley School (California)") prep school. Upending the character's world is the arrival of a mysterious new student, Robert Mallory, whose unsettling presence coincides with the activities of a serial killer known as The Trawler.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Release-3)
