## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Development")]

In April 2023, it was reported that Ellis would write the series based on his novel for [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO"), with Ellis executive producing alongside Nick Hall and Brian Young.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-12) In a June 2023 interview with the Spanish publication _El Independiente_, Ellis had confirmed that [Luca Guadagnino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luca_Guadagnino "Luca Guadagnino") was set to direct the series with Ellis himself saying that he may direct some episodes as well.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) In January 2025, Ellis revealed that the adaptation, which [Kristoffer Borgli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristoffer_Borgli "Kristoffer Borgli") had signed on to direct, was no longer being developed at HBO, following creative differences. In February 2025, [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(producer) "Ryan Murphy (producer)") was revealed to be in closing talks to revive the project at a different network.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-14)

In May 2025, it was announced that [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") was in early development on the series and it would be directed by [Max Winkler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Winkler_(director) "Max Winkler (director)"). It is produced by [20th Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Television "20th Television") in association with Ryan Murphy Television. Murphy, Ellis and Winkler executive produce alongside Nick Hall, Kathleen McCaffrey, [Michael Uppendahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Uppendahl "Michael Uppendahl"), Brian Young, [Alexis Martin Woodall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Martin_Woodall "Alexis Martin Woodall"), [Nina Jacobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Jacobson "Nina Jacobson"), [Brad Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Simpson_(producer) "Brad Simpson (producer)"), [Braxton Pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braxton_Pope "Braxton Pope"), and Tanase Popa.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Release-3)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Gerber-15) In July 2025, the series was officially greenlit.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Series_Order-16) Murphy has talked about a plan for the show to run for at least 3 seasons.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-17)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Casting")]

Prior to the series order, [Jacob Elordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Elordi "Jacob Elordi") was reported to be in talks for a role in the adaption in September 2023. In July 2025, in addition to the greenlight of the show announcement, it was revealed that [Igby Rigney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igby_Rigney "Igby Rigney"), [Homer Gere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer_Gere "Homer Gere"), and [Graham Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Campbell_(actor) "Graham Campbell (actor)") joined the cast as Ellis, Robert Mallory, and Thom Wright respectively.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Series_Order-16) In August 2025, it was revealed that [Hayes Warner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayes_Warner "Hayes Warner") joined the cast as Debbie Schaffer.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-18) In October 2025, [Wes Bentley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Bentley "Wes Bentley") joined the cast as Debbie's father Terry alongside [Evan Rachel Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Rachel_Wood "Evan Rachel Wood") and [Jordan Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Roth "Jordan Roth") who were cast in recurring roles.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-21) In April 2026, it was reported that [Owen Painter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Painter "Owen Painter") had been cast to the series.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-22)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Music")]

In July 2026, it was revealed that [Troye Sivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troye_Sivan "Troye Sivan") and his longtime collaborator [Leland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leland_(musician) "Leland (musician)") contributed the original music for _The Shards_ alongside [Oscar Görres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_G%C3%B6rres "Oscar Görres") and the series star Hayes Warner.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-24) "LA Wants Me Dead" performed by Sivan, and written by him, Leland, and Görres, was released on August 12, 2026.

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Filming")]

Principal photography began in November 2025 and wrapped in March 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-26)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Release")]

In March 2026, [Brad Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Simpson_(producer) "Brad Simpson (producer)") revealed in an interview that _The Shards_ had been aiming for a summer airdate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) In June 2026, it was announced that the series would premiere on August 5, 2026.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-Release-3)[FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") and [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") released the first two episodes of the series on August 5, with the remaining episodes released weekly on Wednesdays through the season finale on September 9.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-28) Internationally, _The Shards_ was made available for streaming on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-29)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On the review aggregator website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 56% of 57 critics' reviews are positive, with an average of rated reviews of 6.3/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "The combination of [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(producer) "Ryan Murphy (producer)") and [Bret Easton Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bret_Easton_Ellis "Bret Easton Ellis") should elicit magnanimously pulpy TV, but instead _The Shards_ relegates itself to obtuse style with mildly entertaining substance."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-RT-30)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 55 out of 100, based on 24 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-31)

### Ratings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Shards_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Ratings")]

On streaming, _The Shards_ ranked No. 2 on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu")'s "Top 15 Today" list—a daily updated list of the platform's most-watched titles—on August 6, the day after its premiere. The series remained on Hulu's "Top 15 Today" list from August 6 through September 18, 2026.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-38) Streaming analytics firm FlixPatrol, which monitors daily updated VOD charts and streaming ratings across the globe, reported that _The Shards_ ranked No. 1 as the most-streamed series worldwide on Disney+ on August 15, 2026. On the same day, the series was notably the most-streamed series on Disney+ in countries including Albania, Australia, Belgium, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, and New Zealand.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shards_(TV_series)#cite_note-39)

_**Blindspotting**_ is an American [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") television series and a [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)")[sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequel "Sequel") of the [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"). Set six months after the events of the film, the series follows Ashley, who is forced to move in with the mother of Miles, her boyfriend and father of her son, after he is suddenly incarcerated. The series co-stars [Jaylen Barron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Barron "Jaylen Barron"), Candace Nicholas-Lippman, Benjamin Earl Turner, and Atticus Woodward.

The series was created and executive produced by [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") and [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs"), writers, producers and lead stars of the original film, with Casal also acting as [showrunner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showrunner "Showrunner"). [Keith Calder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Calder "Keith Calder"), a producer on the original film, is also an executive producer, as well as actress [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones"). It premiered on June 13, 2021 on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz").[[1]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-1) In October 2021, the series was renewed for a second season which premiered on April 14, 2023.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3) In September 2023, the series was canceled after two seasons.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

## Plot

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Six months after the events in the [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"), Miles, Ashley's partner of 12 years and father of their son, is suddenly incarcerated,[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-5) and the situation leaves her to navigate a chaotic and humorous existential crisis when she and her son Sean are forced to move in with Miles' mother and half-sister.[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-6)

## Production

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Development")]

In September 2020, it was announced that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") had ordered a spin-off series of _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ by [Carlos López Estrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_L%C3%B3pez_Estrada "Carlos López Estrada"), with [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones") set to star and produce, with [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs") and [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") serving as executive producers and writers on the series.[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-15) Production companies involved with the series were slated to consist of [Lionsgate Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Television "Lionsgate Television"), Snoot Entertainment, and Barnyard Projects.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-16) In December 2020, Benjamin Earl Turner, Atticus Woodward, Jaylen Barron, Candace Nicholas-Lippman and [Helen Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Hunt "Helen Hunt") joined the cast in starring roles, with Rafael Casal and [Justin Chu Cary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Chu_Cary "Justin Chu Cary") set to appear in recurring capacity.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-17)[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") for the series began in December 2020.[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-19) Production for the first season took place in March 2021 in [West Oakland, Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Oakland,_Oakland,_California "West Oakland, Oakland, California").[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)

Diggs does not reprise his film role as Collin in the first season beyond a voice cameo in the finale, despite co-creating the show. Casal hoped to include Collin during the planning stages, but Diggs wished for the season to focus on Ashley. He ultimately came to regret not making an appearance. Diggs and Casal both expressed interest in bringing back Collin for a potential second season.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-21)

On October 14, 2021, Starz renewed the series for a second season.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2) On April 14, 2022, [LeVar Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeVar_Burton "LeVar Burton"), Katlynn Simone Smith, Tamera Tomakili, and [Tim Chantarangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Chantarangsu "Tim Chantarangsu") were cast in recurring roles, while [E-40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-40 "E-40"), [P-Lo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_HBK_Gang "The HBK Gang") and [Too $hort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too_$hort "Too $hort") were set to guest star for the second season.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Recurandguest-7) Production for the series' sophomore season wrapped on April 28, 2022.[[21]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-22)

It was announced on January 11, 2023 that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") would premiere a number of episodes of their sophomore season at the 2023 [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") Festival held in Austin, Texas in March under the TV Spotlight category.[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)

On September 25, 2023, Starz canceled the series after two seasons.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

### Music

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Music")]

Show creators Rafael Casal and Daveed Diggs recruited fellow schoolmate [Ambrose Akinmusire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambrose_Akinmusire "Ambrose Akinmusire") and _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ film composer [Michael Yezerski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Yezerski "Michael Yezerski") to compose the score for the series. Akinmusire and Yezerski have created score to accompany spoken word, verse, dance, and various other types of scenes demonstrated throughout the series. In a _Variety_ article, Akinmusire and Yezerski describe the experience as "a very rare opportunity for the score to just become the driving language of a piece of dramatic television content."[[23]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-24)

## Release

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Release")]

The series had its world premiere at the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") on June 11, 2021.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Tribeca-9)[[24]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-25) It premiered on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") on June 13, 2021.[[25]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-26) The second season premiered on April 14, 2023.[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3)

## Reception

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the first season holds an approval rating of 100% based on 25 critic reviews, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "The rare adaptation that exceeds its source material, _Blindspotting_ deftly takes on complicated social constructs with comedic flair, crafting a show that's as funny as it is poignant while giving its incredible ensemble—led by the captivating Jasmine Cephas Jones—plenty of room to shine."[[26]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a weighted average score of 76 out of 100, based on 15 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[27]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)

The second season has a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 5 critic reviews, with an average rating of 8.7/10.[[28]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-29)

_**Blindspotting**_ is an American [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") television series and a [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)")[sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequel "Sequel") of the [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"). Set six months after the events of the film, the series follows Ashley, who is forced to move in with the mother of Miles, her boyfriend and father of her son, after he is suddenly incarcerated. The series co-stars [Jaylen Barron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Barron "Jaylen Barron"), Candace Nicholas-Lippman, Benjamin Earl Turner, and Atticus Woodward.

The series was created and executive produced by [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") and [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs"), writers, producers and lead stars of the original film, with Casal also acting as [showrunner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showrunner "Showrunner"). [Keith Calder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Calder "Keith Calder"), a producer on the original film, is also an executive producer, as well as actress [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones"). It premiered on June 13, 2021 on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz").[[1]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-1) In October 2021, the series was renewed for a second season which premiered on April 14, 2023.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3) In September 2023, the series was canceled after two seasons.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

## Plot

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Six months after the events in the [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting"), Miles, Ashley's partner of 12 years and father of their son, is suddenly incarcerated,[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-5) and the situation leaves her to navigate a chaotic and humorous existential crisis when she and her son Sean are forced to move in with Miles' mother and half-sister.[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-6)

## Production

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Development")]

In September 2020, it was announced that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") had ordered a spin-off series of _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ by [Carlos López Estrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_L%C3%B3pez_Estrada "Carlos López Estrada"), with [Jasmine Cephas Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Cephas_Jones "Jasmine Cephas Jones") set to star and produce, with [Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs "Daveed Diggs") and [Rafael Casal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Casal "Rafael Casal") serving as executive producers and writers on the series.[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-15) Production companies involved with the series were slated to consist of [Lionsgate Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Television "Lionsgate Television"), Snoot Entertainment, and Barnyard Projects.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-16) In December 2020, Benjamin Earl Turner, Atticus Woodward, Jaylen Barron, Candace Nicholas-Lippman and [Helen Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Hunt "Helen Hunt") joined the cast in starring roles, with Rafael Casal and [Justin Chu Cary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Chu_Cary "Justin Chu Cary") set to appear in recurring capacity.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-17)[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") for the series began in December 2020.[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-production-18)[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-19) Production for the first season took place in March 2021 in [West Oakland, Oakland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Oakland,_Oakland,_California "West Oakland, Oakland, California").[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-20)

Diggs does not reprise his film role as Collin in the first season beyond a voice cameo in the finale, despite co-creating the show. Casal hoped to include Collin during the planning stages, but Diggs wished for the season to focus on Ashley. He ultimately came to regret not making an appearance. Diggs and Casal both expressed interest in bringing back Collin for a potential second season.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-21)

On October 14, 2021, Starz renewed the series for a second season.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Renewal-2) On April 14, 2022, [LeVar Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeVar_Burton "LeVar Burton"), Katlynn Simone Smith, Tamera Tomakili, and [Tim Chantarangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Chantarangsu "Tim Chantarangsu") were cast in recurring roles, while [E-40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-40 "E-40"), [P-Lo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_HBK_Gang "The HBK Gang") and [Too $hort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too_$hort "Too $hort") were set to guest star for the second season.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Recurandguest-7) Production for the series' sophomore season wrapped on April 28, 2022.[[21]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-22)

It was announced on January 11, 2023 that [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") would premiere a number of episodes of their sophomore season at the 2023 [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") Festival held in Austin, Texas in March under the TV Spotlight category.[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-23)

On September 25, 2023, Starz canceled the series after two seasons.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-4)

### Music

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Music")]

Show creators Rafael Casal and Daveed Diggs recruited fellow schoolmate [Ambrose Akinmusire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambrose_Akinmusire "Ambrose Akinmusire") and _[Blindspotting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting "Blindspotting")_ film composer [Michael Yezerski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Yezerski "Michael Yezerski") to compose the score for the series. Akinmusire and Yezerski have created score to accompany spoken word, verse, dance, and various other types of scenes demonstrated throughout the series. In a _Variety_ article, Akinmusire and Yezerski describe the experience as "a very rare opportunity for the score to just become the driving language of a piece of dramatic television content."[[23]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-24)

## Release

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Release")]

The series had its world premiere at the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") on June 11, 2021.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-Tribeca-9)[[24]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-25) It premiered on [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") on June 13, 2021.[[25]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-26) The second season premiered on April 14, 2023.[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2Premieredate-3)

## Reception

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blindspotting_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the first season holds an approval rating of 100% based on 25 critic reviews, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "The rare adaptation that exceeds its source material, _Blindspotting_ deftly takes on complicated social constructs with comedic flair, crafting a show that's as funny as it is poignant while giving its incredible ensemble—led by the captivating Jasmine Cephas Jones—plenty of room to shine."[[26]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-27) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a weighted average score of 76 out of 100, based on 15 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[27]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-28)

The second season has a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 5 critic reviews, with an average rating of 8.7/10.[[28]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindspotting_(TV_series)#cite_note-29)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American screenwriter and director 

| Aurora Guerrero |
| --- |
| Born | [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), California, U.S. |
| Education | * [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley")([BA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts")) * [California Institute of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Institute_of_the_Arts "California Institute of the Arts")([MFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts")) |
| Occupations | [Film director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter"), [activist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activist "Activist") |

**Aurora Guerrero** is a writer-director from [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-1) As a queer-identifying and Chicana woman from a working-class background, she incorporates the intersection of these identities into her work.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-2) Guerrero's best-known films include _Viernes Girl_ (2005) and _[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_ (2012), which has won several awards.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aurora_Guerrero&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Guerrero was born in the [Mission District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_District,_San_Francisco "Mission District, San Francisco") of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), California, to Mexican immigrant parents, later growing up on the border of the cities of [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_California "Richmond, California") and [El Cerrito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Cerrito,_California "El Cerrito, California") while working at her parents' small Mexican restaurant in [Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley,_California "Berkeley, California"). Guerrero studied both Psychology and [Chicano studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicana/o_studies "Chicana/o studies") at the [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley"), completing a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts"). She later moved to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to study directing at [California Institute of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Institute_of_the_Arts "California Institute of the Arts") in [Santa Clarita, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clarita,_California "Santa Clarita, California") earning a [Master of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-Filmmaker_Magazine-3) It was here she began to examine the intersection of sexuality, race, and class and better connected to parts of her identity.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:3-4) Her narrative work often examines the intersection of the working class, queer people, and people of color.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aurora_Guerrero&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Early in her career, she co-founded Womyn Image Makers (WIM), a queer Xicana-identified film collective based out of Los Angeles [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-6), along with Dalila Mendez, Maritza Alvarez, and Claudia Mercado. As WIM, in 2005, she directed the short film _Pura Lengua_, which debuted at the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival"). Her second short film, _Viernes Girl_, won the 2005 [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")/[New York International Latino Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_International_Latino_Film_Festival "New York International Latino Film Festival") short film competition. [[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-PRNewsWire_-_HBO-7) She was featured on Filmmaker Magazine's "25 Faces to Watch" list as a result of her work, and both films caught the attention of film institutions such as [Sundance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival"), [Tribeca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"), and [Film Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Independent's_Spirit_Awards "Film Independent's Spirit Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5) Guerrero also went on to assist director [Patricia Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Cardoso "Patricia Cardoso") on her debut feature, _[Real Women Have Curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real\_Women\_Have\_Curves "Real Women Have Curves")_, which won the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival")[Audience Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audience_Award "Audience Award") in 2002. In 2005 Guerrero was selected as a Sundance Institute Ford Foundation film fellow.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:3-4) While there, she participated in the Native Indigenous Lab with her script for _[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-Indie_Wire-8) Through collaboration with members of WIM, Guerrero has created a body of work by or about queer women of color not previously featured or circulated in mainstream production houses. Guerrero asserts "third-space feminism" as the directive for her cinematic interventions, as she has been influenced by the rich intellectual genealogy of Chicana feminist theory. [[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-9)

In 2012, Guerrero made her feature film debut at the Sundance Film Festival with _Mosquita y Mari_, becoming the first Chicana filmmaker to debut a feature-length film who was also previously a Sundance Institute and Ford Foundation Fellow.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-CalArts_news-10)_[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_ has since traveled to over 100 film festivals, including [San Francisco International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_International_Film_Festival "San Francisco International Film Festival"), [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Queer_Film_Festival "Melbourne Queer Film Festival"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-11)[Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara_Film_Festival "Guadalajara Film Festival"), [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo"), and has garnered multiple awards, including Best First Feature at [Outfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outfest "Outfest") and Best U.S. Latino Film at New York's [Cinema Tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_Tropical "Cinema Tropical") while picking up [Spirit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_Award "Spirit Award") and [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Award "GLAAD Media Award") nominations for Best First Feature Under 500k and the Piaget's Producer's Award.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5) The film tells the coming-of-age story of two teen Chicanas in [Huntington Park, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Park,_California "Huntington Park, California") who form a relationship ignited by sexual attraction.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-xQsi_Magazine-12)

In 2014, Guerrero announced her next project, _Los Valientes_, about a young undocumented [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans")[gay man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_man "Gay man") living in the U.S.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-13)_Los Valientes_, slated to be Guerrero's second feature, has been awarded two grants by SFF/KRF, a 2014 Sundance Feature Film Development Grant and a 2013 Tribeca Narrative Grant, and was selected to participate in IFP's No Borders Market in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5)

Most of Guerrero's film work has been centered around California, especially the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") where she grew up. Her first work not centered in California was the episode of _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_ she directed, centered in [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:1-14)

In 2017, Guerrero directed the [Ava DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay") produced _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_ episode "What Do I Care for Morning" which aired as episode three in season two. [DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay") chose Guerrero for the directorial position because of her work _[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_. Based on this film, [DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay") felt confident enough that Guerrero could focus on the power of intimacy, especially for _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_, a show that focuses so much on family, betrayal and injustice. Prior to directing episode three of season two of _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_, Guerrero had no idea what episode or what she was going to be directing specifically. Exploring the flirtation, tension, and budding romance of this episode is one of her strengths, and it was a perfect directorial fit for her.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:1-14)

DuVernay later recommended Guerrero to [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda") to direct the music video for [Andra Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andra_Day "Andra Day")'s cover of "Burn" from _[The Hamilton Mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hamilton\_Mixtape "The Hamilton Mixtape")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-15)

In 2020, Guerrero coordinated outreach for the first-ever Latinx Directors Database alongside the founding directors Alberto Belli, Joel Novoa, and Diego Valasco.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:2-16) The website is a resource for interested individuals to discover and learn about the work of Latinx filmmakers and seeks to increase representation in cinema.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:2-16) In discussion of the database, Guerrero mentioned the various perspectives that Latinx creators have to offer and the importance of reducing gaps left by historical patterns of exclusion.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-17)

## Influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aurora_Guerrero&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Influences")]

In a blog post that she wrote on the [Sundance Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Institute "Sundance Institute") website on April 28, 2011[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-Sundance_Institute_Blog-18) Guerrero writes, "My first inspirations were writers. Women of color feminist writers like [Audre Lorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audre_Lorde "Audre Lorde"), Cherrie Moraga, Gloria Anzaldúa, [Chrystos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrystos "Chrystos"), [June Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Jordan "June Jordan"), and [Angela Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Davis "Angela Davis"). When I discovered their brave works as a freshman in college, a fierce creative seed was planted in me. It was a calling I had the moment I was stripped naked by their words." Her work showcases the experiences of [Chicanas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicanas "Chicanas") that often echo her own experiences.

In an interview with [_El Tecolote_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Tecolote_(newspaper) "El Tecolote (newspaper)") on April 26, 2012, Guerrero stressed the importance of “opening doors to Latinos, especially women and youth, behind the camera in order to help build a community of Latina/o artists,” something she didn't have when she was a girl.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-El_Tecolote-19) She also stresses the importance of activity in politics and cultural activism.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5)

**Aurora Guerrero** is a writer-director from [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-1) As a queer-identifying and Chicana woman from a working-class background, she incorporates the intersection of these identities into her work.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-2) Guerrero's best-known films include _Viernes Girl_ (2005) and _[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_ (2012), which has won several awards.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aurora_Guerrero&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Guerrero was born in the [Mission District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_District,_San_Francisco "Mission District, San Francisco") of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), California, to Mexican immigrant parents, later growing up on the border of the cities of [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_California "Richmond, California") and [El Cerrito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Cerrito,_California "El Cerrito, California") while working at her parents' small Mexican restaurant in [Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley,_California "Berkeley, California"). Guerrero studied both Psychology and [Chicano studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicana/o_studies "Chicana/o studies") at the [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley"), completing a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts"). She later moved to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to study directing at [California Institute of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Institute_of_the_Arts "California Institute of the Arts") in [Santa Clarita, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clarita,_California "Santa Clarita, California") earning a [Master of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-Filmmaker_Magazine-3) It was here she began to examine the intersection of sexuality, race, and class and better connected to parts of her identity.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:3-4) Her narrative work often examines the intersection of the working class, queer people, and people of color.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aurora_Guerrero&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Early in her career, she co-founded Womyn Image Makers (WIM), a queer Xicana-identified film collective based out of Los Angeles [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-6), along with Dalila Mendez, Maritza Alvarez, and Claudia Mercado. As WIM, in 2005, she directed the short film _Pura Lengua_, which debuted at the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival"). Her second short film, _Viernes Girl_, won the 2005 [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")/[New York International Latino Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_International_Latino_Film_Festival "New York International Latino Film Festival") short film competition. [[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-PRNewsWire_-_HBO-7) She was featured on Filmmaker Magazine's "25 Faces to Watch" list as a result of her work, and both films caught the attention of film institutions such as [Sundance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival"), [Tribeca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"), and [Film Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Independent's_Spirit_Awards "Film Independent's Spirit Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5) Guerrero also went on to assist director [Patricia Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Cardoso "Patricia Cardoso") on her debut feature, _[Real Women Have Curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real\_Women\_Have\_Curves "Real Women Have Curves")_, which won the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival")[Audience Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audience_Award "Audience Award") in 2002. In 2005 Guerrero was selected as a Sundance Institute Ford Foundation film fellow.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:3-4) While there, she participated in the Native Indigenous Lab with her script for _[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-Indie_Wire-8) Through collaboration with members of WIM, Guerrero has created a body of work by or about queer women of color not previously featured or circulated in mainstream production houses. Guerrero asserts "third-space feminism" as the directive for her cinematic interventions, as she has been influenced by the rich intellectual genealogy of Chicana feminist theory. [[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-9)

In 2012, Guerrero made her feature film debut at the Sundance Film Festival with _Mosquita y Mari_, becoming the first Chicana filmmaker to debut a feature-length film who was also previously a Sundance Institute and Ford Foundation Fellow.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-CalArts_news-10)_[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_ has since traveled to over 100 film festivals, including [San Francisco International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_International_Film_Festival "San Francisco International Film Festival"), [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Queer_Film_Festival "Melbourne Queer Film Festival"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-11)[Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara_Film_Festival "Guadalajara Film Festival"), [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo"), and has garnered multiple awards, including Best First Feature at [Outfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outfest "Outfest") and Best U.S. Latino Film at New York's [Cinema Tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_Tropical "Cinema Tropical") while picking up [Spirit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_Award "Spirit Award") and [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Award "GLAAD Media Award") nominations for Best First Feature Under 500k and the Piaget's Producer's Award.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5) The film tells the coming-of-age story of two teen Chicanas in [Huntington Park, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Park,_California "Huntington Park, California") who form a relationship ignited by sexual attraction.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-xQsi_Magazine-12)

In 2014, Guerrero announced her next project, _Los Valientes_, about a young undocumented [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans")[gay man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_man "Gay man") living in the U.S.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-13)_Los Valientes_, slated to be Guerrero's second feature, has been awarded two grants by SFF/KRF, a 2014 Sundance Feature Film Development Grant and a 2013 Tribeca Narrative Grant, and was selected to participate in IFP's No Borders Market in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5)

Most of Guerrero's film work has been centered around California, especially the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") where she grew up. Her first work not centered in California was the episode of _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_ she directed, centered in [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:1-14)

In 2017, Guerrero directed the [Ava DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay") produced _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_ episode "What Do I Care for Morning" which aired as episode three in season two. [DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay") chose Guerrero for the directorial position because of her work _[Mosquita y Mari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquita\_y\_Mari "Mosquita y Mari")_. Based on this film, [DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay") felt confident enough that Guerrero could focus on the power of intimacy, especially for _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_, a show that focuses so much on family, betrayal and injustice. Prior to directing episode three of season two of _[Queen Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_Sugar "Queen Sugar")_, Guerrero had no idea what episode or what she was going to be directing specifically. Exploring the flirtation, tension, and budding romance of this episode is one of her strengths, and it was a perfect directorial fit for her.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:1-14)

DuVernay later recommended Guerrero to [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda") to direct the music video for [Andra Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andra_Day "Andra Day")'s cover of "Burn" from _[The Hamilton Mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hamilton\_Mixtape "The Hamilton Mixtape")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-15)

In 2020, Guerrero coordinated outreach for the first-ever Latinx Directors Database alongside the founding directors Alberto Belli, Joel Novoa, and Diego Valasco.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:2-16) The website is a resource for interested individuals to discover and learn about the work of Latinx filmmakers and seeks to increase representation in cinema.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:2-16) In discussion of the database, Guerrero mentioned the various perspectives that Latinx creators have to offer and the importance of reducing gaps left by historical patterns of exclusion.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-17)

## Influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aurora_Guerrero&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Influences")]

In a blog post that she wrote on the [Sundance Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Institute "Sundance Institute") website on April 28, 2011[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-Sundance_Institute_Blog-18) Guerrero writes, "My first inspirations were writers. Women of color feminist writers like [Audre Lorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audre_Lorde "Audre Lorde"), Cherrie Moraga, Gloria Anzaldúa, [Chrystos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrystos "Chrystos"), [June Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Jordan "June Jordan"), and [Angela Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Davis "Angela Davis"). When I discovered their brave works as a freshman in college, a fierce creative seed was planted in me. It was a calling I had the moment I was stripped naked by their words." Her work showcases the experiences of [Chicanas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicanas "Chicanas") that often echo her own experiences.

In an interview with [_El Tecolote_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Tecolote_(newspaper) "El Tecolote (newspaper)") on April 26, 2012, Guerrero stressed the importance of “opening doors to Latinos, especially women and youth, behind the camera in order to help build a community of Latina/o artists,” something she didn't have when she was a girl.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-El_Tecolote-19) She also stresses the importance of activity in politics and cultural activism.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Guerrero#cite_note-:0-5)
